senses.chn: （法庭的）开庭，开庭期；（议会等的）会议，会期

ex.en: a session of the UN General Assembly
ex.cn: 一届联合国大会

ex.en: The court is now in session.
ex.cn: 法庭现在正在开庭。

ex.en: The committee met in closed session (= with nobody else present).
ex.cn: 委员会举行了闭门会议。

senses.def: a school or university year
an occasion when people meet to play music, especially Irish music, in a pub/bar
senses.chn: （酒吧里的）演奏会（尤指演奏爱尔兰音乐）

senses.def: a musician who is hired to play on recordings but is not a permanent member of a band
senses.chn: （乐队为录音而雇用的）临时乐师

senses.def: to put sth/sb in a particular place or position

ex.en: She set a tray down on the table.
ex.cn: 她把托盘放到桌上。

ex.en: They ate everything that was set in front of them.
ex.cn: 他们把放在面前的东西都吃光了。

ex.en: The house is set (= located) in fifty acres of parkland.
ex.cn: 房子四周是五十英亩开阔的绿地。

senses.def: to cause sb/sth to be in a particular state; to start sth happening
senses.chn: 使处于某种状况；使开始

ex.en: Her manner immediately set everyone at their ease.
ex.cn: 她的态度立刻使大家感到轻松了。

ex.en: He pulled the lever and set the machine in motion.
ex.cn: 他扳动操纵杆，启动了机器。

ex.en: The hijackers set the hostages free.
ex.cn: 劫机者释放了人质。

ex.en: Her remarks set me thinking.
ex.cn: 她的话引起了我的深思。

senses.def: to place the action of a play, novel or film/movie in a particular place, time, etc.
senses.chn: 把故事情节安排在；以…为…设置背景

ex.en: The novel is set in London in the 1960s.
ex.cn: 这部小说以 20 世纪 60 年代的伦敦为背景。

senses.def: to prepare or arrange sth so that it is ready for use or in position

ex.en: She set the camera on automatic.
ex.cn: 她把照相机调到自动状态。

ex.en: I set my watch by (= make it show the same time as) the TV.
ex.cn: 我按电视对了手表。

ex.en: Set the alarm for 7 o'clock.
ex.cn: 把闹钟设在 7 点。

senses.def: to arrange knives, forks, etc. on a table for a meal

ex.en: Could you set the table for dinner?
ex.cn: 你把餐具摆好，准备开饭，好吗？

ex.en: The table was set for six guests.
ex.cn: 桌上摆放了六位客人的餐具。

senses.def: to put a precious stone into a piece of jewellery

ex.en: She had the sapphire set in a gold ring.
ex.cn: 她请人把蓝宝石镶嵌到一枚金戒指上。

ex.en: Her bracelet was set with emeralds.
ex.cn: 她的手镯上镶有绿宝石。

senses.def: to arrange or fix sth; to decide on sth

ex.en: They haven't set a date for their wedding yet.
ex.cn: 他们还没有确定婚礼日期。

ex.en: The government has set strict limits on public spending this year.
ex.cn: 今年，政府对公共开支规定了严格的限额。

senses.def: to fix sth so that others copy it or try to achieve it

ex.en: This could set a new fashion.
ex.cn: 这或许会开创一种新时尚。

ex.en: They set high standards of customer service.
ex.cn: 他们制订了严格的客户服务标准。

ex.en: I am unwilling to set a precedent.
ex.cn: 我不想开先例。

ex.en: She set a new world record for the high jump.
ex.cn: 她创造了新的跳高世界纪录。

ex.en: I rely on you to set a good example.
ex.cn: 我指望你来树立一个好榜样。

senses.def: to give sb a piece of work, a task, etc.

ex.en: Who will be setting (= writing the questions for) the French exam?
ex.cn: 谁出法语试题？

ex.en: What books have been set (= are to be studied) for the English course?
ex.cn: 英语课指定了要用哪些书？

ex.en: She's set a difficult task for herself.
ex.cn: 她给自己安排了一项艰巨任务。

ex.en: She's set herself a difficult task.
ex.cn: 她给自己安排了一项艰巨任务。

ex.en: I've set myself to finish the job by the end of the month.
ex.cn: 我要求自己在月底以前完成这项工作。

senses.def: to become firm or hard

ex.en: Leave the concrete to set for a few hours.
ex.cn: 让混凝土凝固几小时。

ex.en: The glue had set hard.
ex.cn: 胶已经粘得很紧。

senses.def: to fix your face into a firm expression

ex.en: Her jaw was set in a determined manner.
ex.cn: 她下巴紧绷着，一副决不动摇的样子。

senses.def: to arrange sb's hair while it is wet so that it dries in a particular style

ex.en: She had her hair washed and set.
ex.cn: 她去洗了头，做了发型。

senses.def: to put a broken bone into a fixed position and hold it there, so that it will heal; to heal in this way

ex.en: The surgeon set her broken arm.
ex.cn: 医生给她接上了手臂上的断骨。

senses.def: to use a machine or computer to arrange writing and images on pages in order to prepare a book, newspaper, etc. for printing
to write music to go with words

ex.en: Schubert set many poems to music.
ex.cn: 舒伯特为许多诗歌谱了曲。

senses.def: to go down below the horizon

ex.en: We sat and watched the sun setting.
ex.cn: 我们坐着看太阳渐渐落下去。

senses.def: to attack sb
to start doing sth

ex.en: She set about the business of cleaning the house.
ex.cn: 她动手打扫起房子来。

ex.en: We need to set about finding a solution.
ex.cn: 我们得着手寻找一个解决办法。

senses.def: to make sb oppose a friend, relative, etc.
senses.chn: 使某人反对（朋友、亲人等）

ex.en: She accused her husband of setting the children against her.
ex.cn: 她指责丈夫唆使孩子们跟她作对。

senses.def: to judge sth by comparing good or positive qualities with bad or negative ones

ex.en: Set against the benefits of the new technology, there is also a strong possibility that jobs will be lost.
ex.cn: 权衡利弊，新技术的确有种种好处，但也很可能使一些人失去工作。

senses.def: to record sth as a business cost as a way of reducing the amount of tax you must pay
senses.chn: 把…按营业成本记账以降低（税额）

ex.en: to set capital costs off against tax
ex.cn: 把资金成本按营业成本记账以减税

senses.def: to make sb/sth different from or better than others
senses.chn: 使与众不同；使突出；使优于…

ex.en: Her elegant style sets her apart from other journalists.
ex.cn: 她的高雅风格使她与其他记者截然不同。

senses.def: to keep sth for a special use or purpose

ex.en: Two rooms were set apart for use as libraries.
ex.cn: 留出两个房间作为图书室。

senses.def: to move sth to one side until you need it
senses.chn: 把…放到一旁（或搁到一边）

senses.def: to save or keep money or time for a particular purpose

ex.en: She tries to set aside some money every month.
ex.cn: 她每个月都尽量存点钱。

senses.def: to not consider sth, because other things are more important

ex.en: Let's set aside my personal feelings for now.
ex.cn: 目前咱们就不要顾及我的个人感情了。

senses.def: to state that a decision made by a court is not legally valid
senses.chn: 撤销（法院的判决）；宣布无效

ex.en: The verdict was set aside by the Appeal Court.
ex.cn: 上诉法庭驳回了那个裁决。

senses.def: to delay the progress of sth/sb by a particular time

ex.en: The bad weather set back the building programme by several weeks.
ex.cn: 天气恶劣，建筑计划延误了几个星期。

senses.def: to cost sb a particular amount of money

ex.en: The repairs could set you back over £200.
ex.cn: 这次修理大概得花你 200 多英镑。

senses.def: to place sth, especially a building, at a distance from sth
senses.chn: 使（建筑物等）与…拉开距离

ex.en: The house is set well back from the road.
ex.cn: 这座房子离公路挺远。

senses.def: to stop and allow sb to get off

ex.en: Passengers may be set down and picked up only at the official stops.
ex.cn: 乘客只有在正式车站方可上下车。

senses.def: to write sth down on paper in order to record it
to give sth as a rule, principle, etc.

ex.en: The standards were set down by the governing body.
ex.cn: 这些标准是由管理机构制定的。

senses.def: to start a journey
to present sth or make it known

ex.en: The President set forth his views in a television broadcast.
ex.cn: 总统在电视讲话中阐述了自己的观点。

senses.def: to begin and seem likely to continue

ex.en: The rain seemed to have set in for the day.
ex.cn: 这雨好像要下一天了。

senses.def: to fasten sth into a flat surface so that it does not stick out from it

ex.en: a plaque set into the wall
ex.cn: 嵌在墙上的牌匾

senses.def: to begin a journey

ex.en: We set off for London just after ten.
ex.cn: 刚过十点，我们就动身上伦敦去了。

senses.def: to make a bomb, etc. explode

ex.en: A gang of boys were setting off fireworks in the street.
ex.cn: 一帮男孩子正在街上放烟火。

senses.def: to make an alarm start ringing

ex.en: Opening this door will set off the alarm.
ex.cn: 一开这道门，警铃就会响。

senses.def: to start a process or series of events

ex.en: Panic on the stock market set off a wave of selling.
ex.cn: 股市恐慌引发了一轮抛售潮。

senses.def: to make sth more noticeable or attractive by being placed near it
senses.chn: 衬托；使显得更突出（或更漂亮）

ex.en: That blouse sets off the blue of her eyes.
ex.cn: 那件上衣衬托出了她的蓝眼睛。

senses.def: to make sb start doing sth such as laughing, crying or talking
senses.chn: 使某人笑（或哭、说等）起来

senses.def: to attack sb suddenly

ex.en: I opened the gate, and was immediately set on by a large dog.
ex.cn: 我一开门，一条大狗就迎面扑来。

senses.def: to make a person or an animal attack sb suddenly

ex.en: The farmer threatened to set his dogs on us.
ex.cn: 农场主威胁要放出狗来咬我们。

senses.def: to leave a place and begin a journey

ex.en: They set out on the last stage of their journey.
ex.cn: 他们动身踏上最后一段行程。

senses.def: to begin a job, task, etc. with a particular aim or goal
senses.chn: （怀着目标）开始工作，展开任务

ex.en: She set out to break the world record.
ex.cn: 她一心努力要打破世界纪录。

ex.en: They succeeded in what they set out to do.
ex.cn: 他们实现了既定的目标。

senses.def: to arrange or display things

ex.en: Her work is always very well set out.
ex.cn: 她总是把工作安排得很有条理。

senses.def: to present ideas, facts, etc. in an organized way, in speech or writing

ex.en: He set out his objections to the plan.
ex.cn: 他陈述了他对这个计划的反对意见。

ex.en: She set out the reasons for her resignation in a long letter.
ex.cn: 她写了一封长信说明自己辞职的原因。

senses.def: to begin doing sth in a busy or determined way
senses.chn: 起劲地干起来；毅然开始做

senses.def: to provide sb with the money that they need in order to do sth

ex.en: A bank loan helped to set him up in business.
ex.cn: 他靠一笔银行贷款做起了生意。

senses.def: to make sb healthier, stronger, more lively, etc.
senses.chn: 使更健康（或强壮、活泼等）

ex.en: The break from work really set me up for the new year.
ex.cn: 放下工作稍事休息，的确使我更有精力在新的一年大干一场了。

senses.def: to trick sb, especially by making them appear guilty of sth

ex.en: He denied the charges, saying the police had set him up.
ex.cn: 他否认那些指控，说警察冤枉他了。

senses.def: to build sth or put sth somewhere

ex.en: The police set up roadblocks on routes out of the city.
ex.cn: 警察在城外的路上设置了路障。

senses.def: to make a piece of equipment or a machine ready for use
senses.chn: 安装好，装配好，调试好（设备或机器）

ex.en: She set up her stereo in her bedroom.
ex.cn: 她把立体声音响装在了卧室里。

senses.def: to arrange for sth to happen

ex.en: I've set up a meeting for Friday.
ex.cn: 我已安排好在星期五开会。

senses.def: to create sth or start it

ex.en: to set up a business
ex.cn: 开办公司

ex.en: A fund will be set up for the dead men's families.
ex.cn: 将为死者家属设立一项基金。

senses.def: to start a process or a series of events

ex.en: The slump on Wall Street set up a chain reaction in stock markets around the world.
ex.cn: 华尔街股价暴跌在全球股票市场上引起了连锁反应。

senses.def: to start running a business

ex.en: She took out a bank loan and set up on her own.
ex.cn: 她从银行贷了一笔款，自己干起来了。

ex.en: After leaving college, he set himself up as a freelance photographer.
ex.cn: 大学毕业后，他干起了自由摄影师。

senses.def: a group of similar things that belong together in some way
senses.chn: 一套，一副，一组（类似的东西）

ex.en: a set of six chairs
ex.cn: 六把成套的椅子

ex.en: a complete set of her novels
ex.cn: 一整套她的小说

ex.en: a set of false teeth
ex.cn: 一副假牙

ex.en: a new set of rules to learn
ex.cn: 要学的一套新规则

ex.en: You can borrow my keys—I have a spare set.
ex.cn: 你可以借用我的钥匙，我还有一套。

senses.def: a group of objects used together, for example for playing a game
senses.chn: 一套，一副，一组（配套使用的东西）

ex.en: a chess set
ex.cn: 一副国际象棋

senses.def: a group of people who have similar interests and spend a lot of time together socially
senses.chn: 一伙（或一帮、一群）人；阶层；团伙

ex.en: the smart set (= rich, fashionable people)
ex.cn: 富裕时尚一族

ex.en: Dublin's literary set
ex.cn: 都柏林的文学圈子

senses.def: a piece of equipment for receiving television or radio signals
the scenery used for a play, film/movie, etc.

ex.en: We need volunteers to help build and paint the set.
ex.cn: 我们需要一些自愿帮忙搭建和粉刷布景的人。

senses.def: a place where a play is performed or part of a film/movie is filmed

ex.en: The cast must all be on (the) set by 7 in the morning.
ex.cn: 全体演员必须在早上 7 点钟到场。

senses.def: one section of a match in games such as tennis or volleyball

ex.en: She won in straight sets (= without losing a set).
ex.cn: 她一盘未失，连连得胜。

senses.def: a group of things that have a shared quality

ex.en: set theory
ex.cn: 集论

senses.def: a series of songs or pieces of music that a musician or group performs at a concert
a group of school students with a similar ability in a particular subject
senses.chn: （在某学科上能力相当的）一批学生

ex.en: She's in the top set for French.
ex.cn: 她的法语成绩名列前茅。

senses.def: the way in which sb's face or body is fixed in a particular expression, especially one showing determination

ex.en: She admired the firm set of his jaw.
ex.cn: 她喜欢他那副紧绷着下巴的刚毅神态。

senses.def: an act of arranging hair in a particular style while it is wet

ex.en: A shampoo and set costs £15.
ex.cn: 洗头并做发型共 15 英镑。

senses.def: the state of becoming firm or solid
a young plant, shoot etc. for planting

ex.en: onion sets
ex.cn: 洋葱苗

senses.def: in a particular position

ex.en: a house set in 40 acres of parkland
ex.cn: 一所坐落在一片 40 英亩开阔绿地上的房子

ex.en: He had close-set eyes.
ex.cn: 他的两眼靠得很近。

senses.def: planned or fixed
senses.chn: 安排好的；确定的；固定的

ex.en: Each person was given set jobs to do.
ex.cn: 分配给每个人的工作都是预先确定好的。

ex.en: The school funds a set number of free places.
ex.cn: 学校资助固定数目的免费生。

ex.en: Mornings in our house always follow a set pattern.
ex.cn: 在我们家，每天早上的生活总是遵循一种固定的模式。

senses.def: not likely to change

ex.en: set ideas/opinions/views on how to teach
ex.cn: 不变的教学思想／主张／观点

ex.en: As people get older, they get set in their ways.
ex.cn: 随着年龄的增长，人就积习成性。

senses.def: having a fixed price and a limited choice of dishes

ex.en: a set dinner/lunch/meal
ex.cn: 一份晚餐／午餐套餐；一份套餐

ex.en: Shall we have the set menu?
ex.cn: 我们吃套餐好吗？

senses.def: likely to do sth; ready for sth or to do sth

ex.en: The team looks set for victory.
ex.cn: 看来这个队能赢。

ex.en: Interest rates look set to rise again.
ex.cn: 看样子利率又要提高了。

ex.en: Be set to leave by 10 o'clock.
ex.cn: 做好准备，最晚 10 点钟走。

ex.en: The number of people using mobile phones to purchase goods and services is expected / likely to more than double by the end of 2015.
ex.cn: 到 2015 年年底，使用手机购买商品和服务的人数预计／可能会是现在的两倍多。

ex.en: Experts have predicted / forecast that the number of people using their mobile phones to pay for goods and services should exceed 190 million in 2015.
ex.cn: 专家已经预言，到 2015 年使用手机支付商品和服务费用的人数将超过 1.9 亿。

ex.en: This figure is set to reach 200 million by 2016.
ex.cn: 到 2016 年这个数字可能会达到 2 亿。

senses.def: fixed; not natural

ex.en: a set smile
ex.cn: 僵硬的笑容

ex.en: His face took on a set expression.
ex.cn: 他脸上现出凝滞的神态。

senses.def: to be strongly opposed to sth

ex.en: Why are you so dead set against the idea?
ex.cn: 你为什么那样死命地反对这个主意呢？

senses.def: to want to do or have sth very much; to be determined to do sth
senses.chn: 一心想做；决心做；十分想得到

senses.def: used to tell runners in a race to get ready and then to start

example.en: Her manner immediately set everyone at their ease.
example.cn: 她的态度立刻使大家感到轻松了。

example.en: The hijackers set the hostages free.
example.cn: 劫机者释放了人质。

example.en: Her remarks set me thinking.
example.cn: 她的话引起了我的深思。

example.en: She had the sapphire set in a gold ring.
example.cn: 她请人把蓝宝石镶嵌到一枚金戒指上。

example.en: Her bracelet was set with emeralds.
example.cn: 她的手镯上镶有绿宝石。

example.en: What books have been set (= are to be studied) for the English course?
example.cn: 英语课指定了要用哪些书？

example.en: She's set a difficult task for herself.
example.cn: 她给自己安排了一项艰巨任务。

example.en: She's set herself a difficult task.
example.cn: 她给自己安排了一项艰巨任务。

example.en: I've set myself to finish the job by the end of the month.
example.cn: 我要求自己在月底以前完成这项工作。

example.en: The glue had set hard.
example.cn: 胶已经粘得很紧。

senses.def: to start doing sth

ex.en: She set about the business of cleaning the house.
ex.cn: 她动手打扫起房子来。

ex.en: We need to set about finding a solution.
ex.cn: 我们得着手寻找一个解决办法。

senses.def: to attack sb
to start doing sth

ex.en: She set about the business of cleaning the house.
ex.cn: 她动手打扫起房子来。

ex.en: We need to set about finding a solution.
ex.cn: 我们得着手寻找一个解决办法。

senses.def: a system in which the government pays farmers not to use some of their land for growing crops; the land that the farmers are paid not to use
senses.chn: 退耕补贴制度（由政府补贴，鼓励农民退耕部分耕地）；退耕地

senses.def: a difficulty or problem that delays or prevents sth, or makes a situation worse

ex.en: The team suffered a major setback when their best player was injured.
ex.cn: 最优秀的队员受了伤，使得这支队伍的实力大打折扣。

ex.en: The breakdown in talks represents a temporary setback in the peace process.
ex.cn: 谈判破裂意味着和平进程暂时受阻。

senses.def: a book that students must study for a particular exam
to start a journey
a merchant or banker (= a person who sells goods in large quantities) or banker (= a person with an important job in a bank)
a rich man
a title added to a name to indicate high social status
senses.chn: 塞斯（表示社会地位高的头衔）

senses.def: to begin and seem likely to continue

ex.en: The rain seemed to have set in for the day.
ex.cn: 这雨好像要下一天了。

senses.def: to make sth start burning

ex.en: A spark from the fire had set light to a rug.
ex.cn: 从火炉迸出的火星点燃了地毯。

senses.def: to begin a journey

ex.en: We set off for London just after ten.
ex.cn: 刚过十点，我们就动身上伦敦去了。

senses.def: to leave a place and begin a journey

ex.en: They set out on the last stage of their journey.
ex.cn: 他们动身踏上最后一段行程。

senses.def: to begin a job, task, etc. with a particular aim or goal
senses.chn: （怀着目标）开始工作，展开任务

ex.en: She set out to break the world record.
ex.cn: 她一心努力要打破世界纪录。

ex.cn: 他们实现了既定的目标。

senses.def: a phrase that is always used in the same form

ex.cn: 别管语法，只要把这个作为固定词组来学习即可。

senses.def: to cost sb a particular amount of money

ex.cn: 那个电话把一整套事项安排好了。

a long comfortable seat with a back and arms, for two or more people to sit on

senses.chn: 蹲伏猎狗，雪达犬（体大毛长，有几个品种）

senses.def: a person who sets sth

ex.cn: 命题人

ex.cn: 这场演出真正为艺术创新设立了标杆。

ex.cn: 这家公司再也不能在国内计算机市场上独领风骚了。

ex.cn: 当选总理使她的政治生涯灿烂辉煌。

senses.def: to make it possible for sth to happen; to make sth likely to happen

senses.def: to be very successful and gain the admiration of other people

ex.cn: 他的绘画永远不会引起轰动。

senses.def: a set of surroundings; the place at which sth happens

ex.en: It was the perfect setting for a wonderful Christmas.
ex.cn: 环境气氛无可挑剔，正是一个美好的圣诞节所需要的。

ex.en: An unhappy home environment can affect children's behaviour.
ex.cn: 不幸的家庭环境可能对孩子的行为造成影响。

ex.en: a pleasant working environment
ex.cn: 令人愉快的工作环境

ex.en: The island provided an idyllic setting for the concert.
ex.cn: 这岛为音乐会提供了优美的田园布景。

ex.en: The huts blend in perfectly with their surroundings.
ex.cn: 这些棚屋与周围的环境浑然一体，非常和谐。

senses.def: the place and time at which the action of a play, novel, etc. takes place

ex.en: short stories with a contemporary setting
ex.cn: 以当代生活为背景的短篇小说

senses.def: a position at which the controls on a machine can be set, to set the speed, height, temperature, etc.
senses.chn: （机器上调节速度、高度、温度等的）挡，级，点

ex.cn: 对引擎的性能在不同的挡上做了试验。

ex.cn: 要更改字体的大小，请前往 “设置”。

senses.def: music written to go with a poem, etc.

ex.cn: 舒伯特为歌德的一首诗谱的曲

senses.def: a piece of metal in which a precious stone is fixed to form a piece of jewellery
a complete set of equipment for eating with (knife, fork, spoon, glass, etc.) for one person, arranged on a table
senses.chn: （摆在桌上供一人用的）一套餐具

ex.en: a place setting
ex.cn: 一个座位的整套餐具

senses.def: to put an end to an argument or a disagreement
senses.chn: 结束（争论、争端等）；解决（分歧、纠纷等）

ex.cn: 解决争端／争论／事情

ex.en: It's time you settled your differences with your father.
ex.cn: 现在你该解决同你父亲之间的分歧了。

ex.en: There is pressure on the unions to settle.
ex.cn: 工会组织面临消除纷争的压力。

ex.en: The company has agreed to settle out of court (= come to an agreement without going to court).
ex.cn: 那家公司同意庭外和解。

ex.cn: 一切都定下来了，我们乘九点的航班走。

ex.en: Bob will be there? That settles it. I'm not coming.
ex.cn: 鲍勃会去吗？那好，我就不去了。

ex.en: He had to settle his affairs (= arrange all his personal business) in Paris before he could return home.
ex.cn: 他得把他在巴黎的事情处理好才能回家。

ex.en: It's been settled that we leave on the nine o'clock plane.
ex.cn: 已经定好我们乘坐九点的航班离开。

senses.def: to make a place your permanent home

ex.en: She settled in Vienna after her father's death.
ex.cn: 父亲死后，她就在维也纳定居了。

senses.chn: 殖民；作为移民在殖民地定居

ex.en: This region was settled by the Dutch in the nineteenth century.
ex.cn: 荷兰人于 19 世纪来到这一地区定居。

ex.cn: 埃利舒适地靠着椅背坐下。

ex.en: He settled himself comfortably in his usual chair.
ex.cn: 他在自己惯常坐的椅子上舒舒服服地坐下来。

ex.en: I settled her on the sofa and put a blanket over her.
ex.cn: 我把她放在沙发上安顿好，给她盖了一条毯子。

ex.cn: 她用毯子裹住膝盖。

ex.cn: 婴儿安静不下来。

ex.cn: 我吃了一片药，好镇定一下神经。

ex.cn: 这样你的胃应该就不难受了。

ex.cn: 两只鸟落在篱笆上。

ex.cn: 他的目光落在她脸上。

ex.cn: 包裹里的东西可能在运输途中摇密实了。

ex.cn: 请您先结账再离开旅馆。

ex.cn: 保险公司拒付她提出的索赔款项。

ex.cn: 我来把饭费付给你。

ex.cn: 现在我来付账，咱们以后再算。

ex.cn: “谁做得出这样的事呢？” “也许是结有宿怨的人吧。”

ex.cn: 我舒舒服服地坐下看书。

senses.chn: （在某地）定居下来，过安定的生活

ex.cn: 你打算什么时候成家，安定下来？

ex.cn: 那个班一上课总得过一会儿才能安静下来。

ex.cn: 他们终于开始讨论一些主要问题了。

ex.cn: 最后，他们只好接受平局的结果。

ex.cn: 我真心想要的房子我买不起，所以只得退而求其次了。

senses.def: to make sth more acceptable, organized or successful
senses.chn: 把某事物整顿好；使某事物条理化（或更趋完善）

ex.en: I've got all the information together but it still needs knocking into shape.
ex.cn: 我把材料全都收集齐了，但还需要整理。

senses.def: to express or explain a particular idea, plan, etc.
of any type

ex.en: I don't approve of violence in any shape or form.
ex.cn: 我不赞成任何形式的暴力行为。

senses.def: not having the normal shape

ex.en: The wheel had been twisted out of shape.
ex.cn: 轮子已经扭曲变形了。

senses.def: not in good physical condition
the way things are likely to develop in the future
to develop and become more complete or organized
to dance

ex.en: She spent the whole evening throwing shapes on the dance floor.
ex.cn: 她整晚都在舞池里跳舞。

senses.def: to behave in a way that makes you seem threatening, especially by standing as though you are ready to fight, without actually becoming violent
senses.chn: 作势要打架；摆出气势汹汹的样子

ex.en: The two main investors threw some shapes during the debate.
ex.cn: 两名主要投资人在辩论时剑拔弩张，火药味十足。

ex.en: I was worried he might get violent but he was just throwing shapes.
ex.cn: 我担心他会动手，但他只是虚张声势。

senses.def: to become angry, anxious or upset

ex.en: Don't get bent out of shape about it. It was just a mistake!
ex.cn: 不要为这事烦恼了，那只是一个错误而已！

senses.def: to make sth into a particular shape
senses.chn: 使成为…形状（或样子）；塑造

ex.en: Shape the dough into a ball.
ex.cn: 把和好的面揉成一团。

ex.en: This tool is used for shaping wood.
ex.cn: 这个工具是用来加工木料的。

senses.def: to have an important influence on the way that sb/sth develops
senses.chn: 决定…的形成；影响…的发展

ex.en: His ideas had been shaped by his experiences during the war.
ex.cn: 他的思想深受战时经历的影响。

ex.en: She had a leading role in shaping party policy.
ex.cn: 该党奉行何种政策，她起着主导作用。

senses.def: to prepare to do sth, especially hit or kick sth
senses.chn: 准备（做某动作）；摆好姿势

ex.en: She was shaping to hit her second shot.
ex.cn: 她正准备再一次击球。

senses.def: used to tell sb that if they do not improve, work harder, etc. they will have to leave their job, position, etc.
senses.chn: 不好好干就卷铺盖走人

ex.en: He finally faced up to his drug problem when his band told him to shape up or ship out.
ex.cn: 乐队警告他要么好好干，要么走人，这使他终于正视自己的吸毒问题。

senses.def: to develop in a particular way, especially in a good way

ex.en: Our plans are shaping up nicely (= showing signs that they will be successful).
ex.cn: 我们的计划进行得很好。

senses.def: to improve your behaviour, work harder, etc.

ex.en: If he doesn't shape up, he'll soon be out of a job.
ex.cn: 他要是不改好，很快就会丢饭碗的。

example.en: Shape the dough into a ball.
example.cn: 把和好的面揉成一团。

example.en: This tool is used for shaping wood.
example.cn: 这个工具是用来加工木料的。

senses.def: having the type of shape mentioned

ex.en: a huge balloon shaped like a giant cow
ex.cn: 形似一头巨牛的大气球

ex.en: almond-shaped eyes
ex.cn: 杏眼

ex.en: an L-shaped room
ex.cn: L 形房间

senses.def: not having any definite shape
senses.chn: 无定形的；不成形的；样子不好看的

ex.en: a shapeless sweater
ex.cn: 样子难看的套头衫

senses.def: lacking clear organization
senses.chn: 结构混乱的；条理不清的

ex.en: a shapeless and incoherent story
ex.cn: 结构混乱、情节不连贯的故事

senses.def: having an attractive curved shape
(in stories) a person or an animal that is able to change into other people, animals or things

ex.en: In the film he plays a shape-shifter, who takes the form of people's worst fears.
ex.cn: 他在影片中扮演一个变形人，以别人最恐惧的形象出现。

senses.def: to develop in a particular way, especially in a good way

ex.en: Our plans are shaping up nicely (= showing signs that they will be successful).
ex.cn: 我们的计划进行得很好。

senses.def: to improve your behaviour, work harder, etc.

ex.en: If he doesn't shape up, he'll soon be out of a job.
ex.cn: 他要是不改好，很快就会丢饭碗的。

senses.def: used to tell sb that if they do not improve, work harder, etc. they will have to leave their job, position, etc.
senses.chn: 不好好干就卷铺盖走人

ex.en: He finally faced up to his drug problem when his band told him to shape up or ship out.
ex.cn: 乐队警告他要么好好干，要么走人，这使他终于正视自己的吸毒问题。

senses.def: a piece of broken glass, metal, etc.

ex.en: shards of glass
ex.cn: 玻璃碎片

senses.def: to have or use sth at the same time as sb else

ex.en: Sue shares a house with three other students.
ex.cn: 苏和另外三个学生合住一所房子。

ex.en: There isn't an empty table. Would you mind sharing?
ex.cn: 没有空桌子了。你愿不愿意和别人合用？

senses.def: to divide sth between two or more people

ex.en: We shared the pizza between the four of us.
ex.cn: 我们四个人把那份比萨饼分着吃了。

senses.def: to give some of what you have to sb else; to let sb use sth that is yours

ex.en: Eli shared his chocolate with the other kids.
ex.cn: 伊莱把他的巧克力和其他孩子一起分着吃了。

ex.en: The conference is a good place to share information and exchange ideas.
ex.cn: 研讨会是互通信息、交流思想的好场所。

ex.en: John had no brothers or sisters and wasn't used to sharing.
ex.cn: 约翰没有兄弟姐妹，所以不习惯和他人分享东西。

senses.def: to have the same feelings, ideas, experiences, etc. as sb else
senses.chn: 有同样的感情（或想法、经历等）

ex.en: They shared a common interest in botany.
ex.cn: 他们都对植物学感兴趣。

ex.en: a view that is widely shared
ex.cn: 一种得到广泛认同的观点

ex.en: shared values
ex.cn: 共同的价值观

ex.en: People often share their political views with their parents.
ex.cn: 人常常跟自己的父母政治观点一致。

ex.en: I didn't really share in her love of animals.
ex.cn: 我并不怎么像她那样喜欢动物。

senses.def: to tell other people about your ideas, experiences and feelings
senses.chn: 把自己的想法（或经历、感情）告诉（某人）

ex.en: Men often don't like to share their problems.
ex.cn: 男人往往不喜欢把自己的问题告诉他人。

ex.en: The two friends shared everything—they had no secrets.
ex.cn: 这两位朋友无话不谈，彼此之间毫无秘密。

ex.en: Please share this on Facebook and Twitter so we can get the word out.
ex.cn: 请把这个在脸书和推特上分享，好让更多人知道。

ex.en: Would you like to share your experience with the rest of the group?
ex.cn: 你愿意把你的经验与组里其他人分享吗？

ex.en: The group listens while one person shares (= tells other people about their experiences, feelings, etc.).
ex.cn: 一个人在谈自己的情况时，小组的其他成员都听着。

senses.def: to be equally involved in sth or responsible for sth

ex.en: I try to get the kids to share in the housework.
ex.cn: 我尽量让孩子们分担家务活儿。

ex.en: Both drivers shared the blame for the accident.
ex.cn: 事故责任由两个驾车人共同承担。

senses.def: used to say that everyone should share things equally and in a fair way
if you talk to sb about your problems and worries, instead of keeping them to yourself, they seem less serious
senses.chn: 诉说烦恼，一半自消（向人倾诉，愁苦就会减少）

senses.def: one part of sth that is divided between two or more people

ex.en: How much was your share of the winnings?
ex.cn: 在赢的钱里你那份有多少？

ex.en: Next year we hope to have a bigger share of the market.
ex.cn: 明年我们希望获得更大的市场份额。

ex.en: I'm looking for a flat share (= a flat that is shared by two or more people who are not related).
ex.cn: 我想找一套合租公寓。

senses.def: the part that sb has in a particular activity that involves several people
senses.chn: （在多人参加的活动中所占的）一份

ex.en: We all did our share.
ex.cn: 我们都尽力了。

ex.en: Everyone must accept their share of the blame.
ex.cn: 每个人都必须承担自己那份责任。

senses.def: an amount of sth that is thought to be normal or acceptable for one person
senses.chn: 正常的一份；可接受的一份

ex.en: I've had my share of luck in the past.
ex.cn: 以前，命运也不算亏待我。

ex.en: I've done my share of worrying for one day!
ex.cn: 就这一天而论，我操够了心！

senses.def: any of the units of equal value into which a company is divided and sold to raise money. People who own shares receive part of the company's profits.

ex.en: shares in British Telecom
ex.cn: 英国电信公司的股份

ex.en: a fall in share prices
ex.cn: 股票价格的跌落

senses.def: a share of the available money or benefits that you believe you have a right to
senses.chn: 应分得的一份钱财（或好处）

senses.def: (more than) an amount of sth that is considered to be reasonable or acceptable
senses.chn: （超过）合理的数量，恰当的数量

ex.en: He has more than his fair share of problems.
ex.cn: 他的问题过多。

ex.en: I've had my fair share of success in the past.
ex.cn: 过去我已经取得了应有的成功。

senses.def: the largest or best part of sth when it is divided
a share of sth such as money, profits, etc.

example.en: They shared a common interest in botany.
example.cn: 他们都对植物学感兴趣。

example.en: People often share their political views with their parents.
example.cn: 人常常跟自己的父母政治观点一致。

example.en: I didn't really share in her love of animals.
example.cn: 我并不怎么像她那样喜欢动物。

example.en: Would you like to share your experience with the rest of the group?
example.cn: 你愿意把你的经验与组里其他人分享吗？

example.en: Both drivers shared the blame for the accident.
example.cn: 事故责任由两个驾车人共同承担。

example.en: Everyone must accept their share of the blame.
example.cn: 每个人都必须承担自己那份责任。

senses.def: used to say that everyone should share things equally and in a fair way
a farmer who gives part of his or her crop as rent to the owner of the land
an owner of shares in a company or business
the amount of a company or business that sb owns in the form of shares
a list that shows the current value of shares on the stock market, based on the prices of shares of particular companies
a right given to employees to buy shares in their company at a fixed price
senses.chn: 股票期权，认股选择权（让员工可按固定价格购买所属公司的股票）

senses.def: an act of dividing sth between two or more people; the amount of sth that one person receives when it is divided
computer software (= programs, etc.) that is available free for a user to test, after which they must pay if they wish to continue using it
the system of religious laws that Muslims follow
a large sea fish with very sharp teeth and a pointed fin on its back. There are several types of shark, some of which can attack people swimming.
a person who is dishonest in business, especially sb who gives bad advice and gets people to pay too much for sth
having a fine edge or point, especially of sth that can cut or make a hole in sth

ex.en: a sharp knife
ex.cn: 锋利的刀

ex.en: sharp teeth
ex.cn: 锋利的牙齿

senses.def: sudden and rapid, especially of a change in sth

ex.en: a sharp drop in prices
ex.cn: 价格的骤降

ex.en: a sharp rise in crime
ex.cn: 犯罪率的急剧上升

ex.en: a sharp increase in unemployment
ex.cn: 失业人数的剧增

ex.en: He heard a sharp intake of breath.
ex.cn: 他听到猛地倒吸一口气的声音。

ex.en: We need to give young criminals a short, sharp shock (= a punishment that is very unpleasant for a short time).
ex.cn: 对青少年罪犯我们需要给以短暂但严厉的惩处。

senses.def: clear and definite
senses.chn: 清楚明确的；清晰的；鲜明的

ex.en: a sharp outline
ex.cn: 清晰的轮廓

ex.en: The photograph is not very sharp (= there are no clear contrasts between areas of light and shade).
ex.cn: 这张照片不是很清晰。

ex.en: She drew a sharp distinction between domestic and international politics.
ex.cn: 她将国内政治和国际政治截然分开。

ex.en: In sharp contrast to her mood, the clouds were breaking up to reveal a blue sky.
ex.cn: 乌云渐渐散开，露出了蓝天，这和她的情绪形成了鲜明的对照。

ex.en: The issue must be brought into sharper focus.
ex.cn: 必须更集中关注这个问题。

senses.def: quick to notice or understand things or to react

ex.en: to have sharp eyes
ex.cn: 有敏锐的眼睛

ex.en: a girl of sharp intelligence
ex.cn: 聪颖的女孩

ex.en: a sharp sense of humour
ex.cn: 很强的幽默感

ex.en: He kept a sharp lookout for any strangers.
ex.cn: 他警惕地守望着，不放过任何一个陌生人。

ex.en: It was very sharp of you to see that!
ex.cn: 你能看到这一点，很有洞察力！

senses.def: critical or severe

ex.en: sharp criticism
ex.cn: 尖锐的批评

ex.en: Emma has a sharp tongue (= she often speaks in an unpleasant or unkind way).
ex.cn: 埃玛说话尖刻。

ex.en: He was very sharp with me when I was late.
ex.cn: 我迟到了，让他狠狠训了一通。

senses.def: loud, sudden and often high in tone

ex.en: She read out the list in sharp, clipped tones.
ex.cn: 她清脆快速地宣读了名单。

ex.en: There was a sharp knock on the door.
ex.cn: 敲门声大作。

senses.def: very strong and sudden, often like being cut or wounded
senses.chn: （常指受伤似的）剧烈的，猛烈的

ex.en: He winced as a sharp pain shot through his leg.
ex.cn: 腿上一阵剧痛，疼得他龇牙咧嘴。

ex.en: Polly felt a sharp pang of jealousy.
ex.cn: 波利感到一阵强烈的嫉妒。

senses.def: changing direction suddenly

ex.en: a sharp bend in the road
ex.cn: 公路上的急转弯

ex.en: a sharp turn to the left
ex.cn: 向左的急转

senses.def: strong and slightly bitter
senses.chn: 强烈略苦的；辛辣的；刺鼻的

ex.en: The cheese has a distinctively sharp taste.
ex.cn: 这奶酪味道很冲。

ex.en: the pungent smell of burning rubber
ex.cn: 烧橡胶的刺鼻气味

ex.en: Too much pulp produces a sour wine.
ex.cn: 过多的果肉会让酒变酸。

ex.en: acrid smoke from burning tyres
ex.cn: 燃烧轮胎产生的熏烟

ex.en: The cheese has a distinctively sharp taste.
ex.cn: 这奶酪味道很冲。

senses.def: used to describe a very cold or very severe frost or wind
clever but possibly dishonest

ex.en: His lawyer's a sharp operator.
ex.cn: 他的律师是个老狐狸。

ex.en: The firm had to face some sharp practice from competing companies.
ex.cn: 公司不得不面对竞争对手们的小动作。

senses.def: fashionable and new

ex.en: The consultants were a group of men in sharp suits.
ex.cn: 顾问都是些衣着入时的男人。

ex.en: Todd is a sharp dresser.
ex.cn: 托德衣着时髦。

senses.def: not full or round in shape

ex.en: a man with a thin face and sharp features (= a pointed nose and chin)
ex.cn: 脸瘦而棱角分明的男人

senses.def: used after the name of a note to mean a note a semitone/ half step higher

ex.en: the Piano Sonata in C sharp minor
ex.cn: 升 C 小调钢琴奏鸣曲

senses.def: above the correct pitch (= how high or low a note sounds)

ex.en: That note sounded sharp.
ex.cn: 这个音听着偏高。

senses.def: used in orders to tell sb to be quick or to hurry

ex.en: You'd better look sharp or you'll be late.
ex.cn: 你得快点，不然就迟到了。

senses.def: not intelligent

ex.en: He's not exactly the sharpest knife in the drawer, is he?
ex.cn: 他的脑子不灵活，是不是？

senses.def: the place or position of greatest difficulty or responsibility
senses.chn: 最为困难（或责任极其重大）的地方（或职位）

ex.en: He started work at the sharp end of the business, as a salesman.
ex.cn: 他从这一行最为棘手的工作做起，当了推销员。

senses.def: used after an expression for a time of day to mean 'exactly'
senses.chn: （用于表时间的词语后，表示准时）…整

ex.en: Please be here at seven o'clock sharp.
ex.cn: 请七点整到这里。

senses.def: turning suddenly to the left or right
above the correct pitch (= how high or low a note sounds)
a note played a semitone/ half step higher than the note that is named. The written symbol is (♯)

ex.en: It's a difficult piece to play, full of sharps and flats.
ex.cn: 这支乐曲不好演奏，到处是升降记号。

senses.def: things with a sharp edge or point, such as needles and syringes
senses.chn: 锐利的东西（如针、注射器等）

ex.en: the safe disposal of sharps
ex.cn: 对有利刃或尖刺的东西的安全处置

example.en: He was very sharp with me when I was late.
example.cn: 我迟到了，让他狠狠训了一通。

senses.def: to make sth sharper; to become sharper

ex.en: This knife needs sharpening.
ex.cn: 这把刀需要磨了。

ex.en: The outline of the trees sharpened as it grew lighter.
ex.cn: 随着天色转亮，树的轮廓变得清晰了。

senses.def: if a sense or feeling sharpens or sth sharpens it, it becomes stronger and/or clearer
senses.chn: （使感觉或感情）加强，加重，变得更明显

ex.en: The sea air sharpened our appetites.
ex.cn: 海上的空气增进了我们的食欲。

senses.def: to make a disagreement between people, or an issue on which people disagree, clearer and more likely to produce a result

ex.en: There is a need to sharpen the focus of the discussion.
ex.cn: 有必要使讨论的焦点更加集中。

senses.def: to become or make sth better, more skilful, more effective, etc. than before

ex.en: He needs to sharpen up before the Olympic trials.
ex.cn: 在奥运会选拔赛之前，他需要进一步磨砺自己。

ex.en: She's doing a course to sharpen her business skills.
ex.cn: 她正进修，以提高自己的业务技能。

senses.def: if your voice sharpens or sth sharpens it, it becomes high and loud in an unpleasant way

example.en: He needs to sharpen up before the Olympic trials.
example.cn: 在奥运会选拔赛之前，他需要进一步磨砺自己。

example.en: She's doing a course to sharpen her business skills.
example.cn: 她正进修，以提高自己的业务技能。

senses.def: a tool or machine that makes things sharp

ex.en: a pencil sharpener
ex.cn: 卷笔刀

ex.en: a knife sharpener
ex.cn: 磨刀石

senses.def: able to see very well and quick to notice things

ex.en: A sharp-eyed reader spotted the mistake in yesterday's paper.
ex.cn: 一个眼尖的读者发现了昨天报纸上的错误。

senses.def: quickly; in a short time
in a critical, rough or severe way

ex.en: The report was sharply critical of the police.
ex.cn: 报道猛烈地抨击了警方。

ex.en: 'Is there a problem?' he asked sharply.
ex.cn: “有问题吗？” 他厉声喝问。

senses.def: suddenly and by a large amount

ex.en: Profits fell sharply following the takeover.
ex.cn: 接管后，利润突然大幅度降低。

ex.en: The road fell sharply to the sea.
ex.cn: 公路陡然下坡，通向大海。

senses.def: in a way that clearly shows the differences between two things

ex.en: Their experiences contrast sharply with those of other children.
ex.cn: 他们的经历和其他孩子的经历形成鲜明的对比。

senses.def: quickly and suddenly or loudly
senses.chn: 迅疾而突然地；急促而大声地

ex.en: She moved sharply across the room to block his exit.
ex.cn: 她疾步冲到门口，挡住他的去路。

ex.en: He rapped sharply on the window.
ex.cn: 他猛敲窗户。

senses.def: used to emphasize that sth has a sharp point or edge

ex.en: sharply pointed
ex.cn: 尖尖的

senses.def: used to express approval or agreement
used as a greeting when people meet or part
a person who is skilled at shooting a gun
to suddenly break into small pieces; to make sth suddenly break into small pieces

ex.en: He dropped the vase and it shattered into pieces on the floor.
ex.cn: 他失手把花瓶掉到地板上摔碎了。

ex.en: the sound of shattering glass
ex.cn: 玻璃破碎的声音

ex.en: The explosion shattered all the windows in the building.
ex.cn: 大楼所有的玻璃都在爆炸中震碎了。

senses.def: to destroy sth completely, especially sb's feelings, hopes or beliefs; to be destroyed in this way
senses.chn: （使感情、希望或信念等）粉碎，破灭；被粉碎；被破坏

ex.en: Anna's self-confidence had been completely shattered.
ex.cn: 安娜的自信心彻底崩溃了。

ex.en: Her experience of divorce shattered her illusions about love.
ex.cn: 她的离婚经历使她对爱情的幻想破灭了。

ex.en: My whole world shattered into a million pieces.
ex.cn: 我的整个世界全塌了。

senses.def: to make sb feel extremely shocked and upset
senses.chn: 使极为惊愕难过；给予极大打击

ex.en: The unexpected death of their son shattered them.
ex.cn: 儿子的意外死亡给他们带来沉重的打击。

example.en: He dropped the vase and it shattered into pieces on the floor.
example.cn: 他失手把花瓶掉到地板上摔碎了。

example.en: The explosion shattered all the windows in the building.

senses.chn: 短暂而美好；简明扼要；紧凑

ex.en: We haven't much time so I'll keep it short and sweet.
ex.cn: 我们时间不多，我就长话短说吧。

senses.def: used to say that it is not worth wasting time doing sth that you dislike or that is not important
senses.chn: 人生苦短；不可枉费此生

senses.def: used when you are saying that you will get to the point of what you are saying quickly, without including all the details
senses.chn: 长话短说；扼要地说；简而言之

senses.def: the whole of sth or less of sth than you expect or should have

ex.en: We experienced the full measure of their hospitality.
ex.cn: 我们领受了他们十足的盛情。

ex.en: The concert only lasted an hour, so we felt we were getting short measure.
ex.cn: 音乐会仅仅持续了一个小时，让我们有一种缺斤少两的感觉。

senses.def: not long in advance; without warning or time for preparation
senses.chn: 随时；一经通知立即；没有准备时间

ex.en: This was the best room we could get at such short notice.
ex.cn: 这是我们临时能弄到的最好的房间了。

ex.en: You must be ready to leave at a moment's notice.
ex.cn: 你必须随时准备出发。

senses.def: used to describe what will happen a long, short, etc. time in the future

ex.en: Such a development seems unlikely, at least in the short term (= it will not happen for quite a long time).
ex.cn: 发生这样的情况看来可能性不大，起码短期之内应当如此。

senses.def: very stupid
senses.chn: 笨得像木头人；笨到极点

senses.def: if you go short of or run short of sth, you do not have enough of it

ex.en: I'd never let you go short of anything.
ex.cn: 我什么都不会让你缺的。

ex.en: Mothers regularly go short of food to ensure their children have enough.
ex.cn: 为了保证自己的孩子吃饱饭，做母亲的经常忍饥挨饿。

ex.en: They had run short of (= used most of their supply of) fuel.
ex.cn: 他们燃料不够用了。

senses.def: not as far as you need or expect

ex.en: All too often you pitch the ball short.
ex.cn: 你投球老是距离不够。

senses.def: before the time expected or arranged; before the natural time

ex.en: a career tragically cut short by illness
ex.cn: 因病不幸中断的事业

ex.en: I'm afraid I'm going to have to stop you short there, as time is running out.
ex.cn: 时间快到了，恐怕我得就此打断你了。

senses.def: to suddenly feel an urgent need to go to the toilet/bathroom
senses.chn: 突然感觉要上厕所；内急

senses.def: to be put at a disadvantage
to have an accident; to get into trouble
to fail to reach the standard that you expected or need

ex.en: The hotel fell far short of their expectations.
ex.cn: 旅馆远没有他们预期的那么好。

senses.def: without sth; without doing sth; unless sth happens

ex.en: Short of a miracle, we're certain to lose.
ex.cn: 除非发生奇迹，否则我们输定了。

ex.en: Short of asking her to leave (= and we don't want to do that) there's not a lot we can do about the situation.
ex.cn: 要是不请她走，我们也就没有多少办法应付这种局面了。

senses.def: to make sb suddenly stop what they are doing

ex.en: I was brought up short by a terrible thought.
ex.cn: 一个可怕的念头闪过，我一下子愣住了。

senses.def: to not value sb/yourself highly enough and show this by the way you treat or present them/yourself
senses.chn: 低估，轻视，小瞧（某人或自己）

senses.def: to suddenly stop, or make sb suddenly stop, doing sth

ex.en: He stopped short when he heard his name.
ex.cn: 听见有人喊他的名字，他突然停住了。

senses.def: to be unwilling to do sth because it may involve a risk, but to nearly do it
senses.chn: 差一点儿没做某事；险些做出某事

ex.en: She stopped short of calling the president a liar.
ex.cn: 她差一点儿没说总统是骗子。

senses.def: a small strong alcoholic drink, for example of whisky
a short film/movie, especially one that is shown before the main film
senses.chn: （尤指在正片前放映的）电影短片

senses.def: in a few words

ex.en: His novels belong to a great but vanished age. They are, in short, old-fashioned.
ex.cn: 他的小说属于一个辉煌但已逝去的时代。一句话，已经过时了。

senses.def: used when you are telling sb the essential facts about sth or what effect it will have, without explaining all the details
a situation when there is not enough of the people or things that are needed

ex.en: food/housing/water shortages
ex.cn: 食物／住房／用水短缺

ex.en: a shortage of funds
ex.cn: 资金不足

ex.en: There is no shortage of (= there are plenty of) things to do in the town.
ex.cn: 城里不愁找不到活儿干。

senses.def: pleasant but not lasting a long time
senses.chn: 短暂而美好；简明扼要；紧凑

ex.en: We haven't much time so I'll keep it short and sweet.
ex.cn: 我们时间不多，我就长话短说吧。

senses.def: a person who is not very tall
a way of cutting a man's hair so that the hair is very short at the sides and the back of the head
senses.chn: 盖式发型（脑后和两侧均剪得很短的男式发型）

senses.def: a rich crisp biscuit/cookie made with flour, sugar and a lot of butter
a cake with a pastry base and cream and fruit on top

ex.en: strawberry shortcake
ex.cn: 草莓酥饼

senses.def: to give back less than the correct amount of money to sb who has paid for sth with more than the exact price

ex.en: I think I've been short-changed at the bar.
ex.cn: 我觉得酒吧没给我找够零钱。

senses.def: to treat sb unfairly by not giving them what they have earned or deserve
a failure in an electrical circuit, when electricity travels along the wrong route because of damaged wires or a fault in the connections between the wires
to have a short circuit; to make sth have a short circuit

ex.en: The wires had short-circuited and burnt out.
ex.cn: 电线短路，烧坏了。

senses.def: to succeed in doing sth more quickly than usual, without going through all the usual processes
a fault in sb's character, a plan, a system, etc.
a type of pastry that crumbles easily, used for making pies, etc.
a quicker or shorter way of getting to a place

ex.en: You can take a shortcut across the field.
ex.cn: 你可以抄近道从田里穿过去。

senses.def: a way of doing sth that is quicker than the usual way

ex.en: There are no shortcuts to economic recovery.
ex.cn: 经济复苏没有捷径可走。

senses.def: to make sth shorter; to become shorter

ex.en: Injury problems could shorten his career.
ex.cn: 受伤的问题有可能缩短他的职业生涯。

ex.en: a shortened version of the game
ex.cn: 简化了的比赛

ex.en: In November the temperatures drop and the days shorten.
ex.cn: 十一月气温下降，白天变短。

ex.en: Her name's Katherine, generally shortened to Kay.
ex.cn: 她名叫凯瑟琳，通常简称凯。

example.en: Injury problems could shorten his career.
example.cn: 受伤的问题有可能缩短他的职业生涯。

example.en: Her name's Katherine, generally shortened to Kay.
example.cn: 她名叫凯瑟琳，通常简称凯。

senses.def: fat that is used for making pastry
if there is a shortfall in sth, there is less of it than you need or expect
likely to become angry very easily
a breed of cat with short hair
a quick way of writing using special signs or abbreviations, used especially to record what sb is saying

ex.en: typing and shorthand
ex.cn: 打字和速记

ex.en: to take sth down in shorthand
ex.cn: 用速记记录某事

ex.en: a shorthand typist
ex.cn: 速记打字员

senses.def: a shorter way of saying or referring to sth, which may not be as accurate as the more complicated way of saying it
not having as many workers or people who can help as you need
that involves transporting people or goods over short distances, especially by plane
a breed of cow with short horns
a small number of candidates for a job, etc., who have been chosen from all the people who applied

ex.en: to draw up a shortlist
ex.cn: 拟就入围名单

ex.en: a shortlist for a literary prize
ex.cn: 一项文学奖的入围名单

ex.en: She is on my shortlist of great singers.
ex.cn: 她是我心目中的优秀歌唱家之一。

senses.def: to put sb/sth on a shortlist for a job, prize, etc.

ex.en: Candidates who are shortlisted for interview will be contacted by the end of the week.
ex.cn: 入围参加面试的求职者将在周末以前得到通知。

senses.def: lasting only for a short time
a short time; not long

ex.en: She arrived shortly after us.
ex.cn: 我们刚到不多会儿她就到了。

ex.en: I saw him shortly before he died.
ex.cn: 在他去世前不久我还见过他一面。

senses.def: soon

ex.en: I'll be ready shortly.
ex.cn: 我马上就准备好了。

senses.def: in an angry and impatient way
a person who works in a restaurant cooking food that can be prepared quickly
designed to travel only over short distances

ex.en: short-range missiles
ex.cn: 短程导弹

senses.def: connected with a short period of time in the future

ex.en: a short-range weather forecast
ex.cn: 短期天气预报

senses.def: short trousers/pants that end above or at the knee

ex.en: a pair of tennis shorts
ex.cn: 一条网球短裤

ex.en: He was wearing a T-shirt and shorts.
ex.cn: 他穿着 T 恤衫和短裤。

senses.def: able to see things clearly only if they are very close to you
not thinking carefully about the possible effects of sth or what might happen in the future

ex.en: a short-sighted policy
ex.cn: 目光短浅的政策

senses.def: a lack of careful thought about the possible effects of sth or what might happen in the future

ex.en: Many people accused the government of short-sightedness.
ex.cn: 很多人指责政府缺乏远见。

senses.def: the ability to see things clearly only if they are very close to you
having fewer members of staff than you need or usually have
senses.chn: 人员配备不足；人手短缺

senses.def: where you only stay for a short time

ex.en: a short-stay car park
ex.cn: 短时停车场

senses.def: a story, usually about imaginary characters and events, that is short enough to be read from beginning to end without stopping
a tendency to become angry very quickly and easily
lasting a short time; designed only for a short period of time in the future

ex.en: a short-term loan
ex.cn: 短期贷款

ex.en: to find work on a short-term contract
ex.cn: 找一份短期合同工作

ex.en: short-term plans
ex.cn: 近期计划

ex.en: a short-term solution to the problem
ex.cn: 解决这个问题的短期措施

ex.en: His short-term memory (= the ability to remember things that happened a short time ago) is failing.
ex.cn: 他的短时记忆越来越差了。

senses.def: a way of thinking or planning that is concerned with the advantages or profits you could have now, rather than the effects in the future
senses.chn: 只注重短期效益的思维方式

senses.def: if workers are put on short time, they work for fewer hours than usual, because there is not enough work to do or not enough money to pay them
a radio wave that has a frequency between 3 and 30 megahertz
a person who is shorter than average
a member of a Native American people many of whom now live in the US state of Wyoming
senses.chn: 肖肖尼人（美洲土著，很多现居于美国怀俄明州）

senses.def: the act of firing a gun; the sound this makes
senses.chn: 射击；开枪（或炮）；枪（或炮）声

ex.en: The man fired several shots from his pistol.
ex.cn: 那个男人用手枪开了几枪。

ex.en: Someone took a shot at the car.
ex.cn: 有人朝轿车开了一枪。

ex.en: We heard some shots in the distance.
ex.cn: 我们听见远处有几声枪响。

senses.def: a person who shoots a gun in a particular way (well, badly, etc.)
senses.chn: 优秀（或不高明等的）射手，枪手，炮手

senses.def: a large number of small metal balls that you fire together from a shotgun
a large stone or metal ball that was shot from a cannon or large gun in the past
senses.chn: （旧时用大炮发射的石质或金属的）弹丸

senses.def: a remark or an action that is usually one of a series, and is aimed against sb/sth that you are arguing or competing with
senses.chn: （针对对手、多为一系列之一的）一席话，一击

ex.en: This statement was the opening shot in the argument.
ex.cn: 这番话打响了争论的第一炮。

ex.en: The supermarket fired the first shot in a price war today.
ex.cn: 今天，这家超市打响了价格战的头一炮。

senses.def: the act of trying to do or achieve sth

ex.en: The team are looking good for a shot at the title.
ex.cn: 看来这个队力争夺冠的势头不错。

ex.en: I've never produced a play before but I'll have a shot at it.
ex.cn: 我从来没有制作过一出戏剧，不过我要尝试一下。

ex.en: I'm willing to give it a shot.
ex.cn: 我愿意试试。

ex.en: Just give it your best shot (= try as hard as you can) and you'll be fine.
ex.cn: 只要尽自己最大努力，你就会有好的结果。

senses.def: the action of hitting, kicking or throwing the ball in order to score a point or goal in a game

ex.en: Taylor scored with a low shot into the corner of the net.
ex.cn: 泰勒一脚低射，把球射入网角。

ex.en: Good shot!
ex.cn: 好球！

senses.def: the heavy ball that is used in the sports competition called shot-put
a photograph

ex.en: I got some good shots of people at the party.
ex.cn: 我给参加聚会的人拍了几张精彩的照片。

ex.en: a photograph of the house
ex.cn: 这座房子的照片

ex.en: Can I take a photograph?
ex.cn: 我可以拍个照吗？

ex.en: We had our picture taken in front of the hotel.
ex.cn: 我们在旅馆前照了相。

ex.en: a passport photo
ex.cn: 护照照片

ex.en: I tried to get a shot of him in the water.
ex.cn: 我试着给他拍一张在水中的照片。

senses.def: a scene in a film/movie that is filmed continuously by one camera

ex.en: the opening shot of a character walking across a desert
ex.cn: 影片开头呈现一个人穿越沙漠的镜头

senses.def: a small amount of a drug that is put into your body using a syringe

ex.en: a flu shot (= to protect you against flu)
ex.cn: 打预防流感的针

ex.en: a shot of morphine
ex.cn: 打一针吗啡

senses.def: a small amount of a drink, especially a strong alcoholic one
senses.chn: 少量饮料；（尤指）少量烈酒

ex.en: a shot of whisky
ex.cn: 一点威士忌

senses.def: an occasion when a spacecraft is sent into space

ex.en: The space shot was shown live on television.
ex.cn: 此次太空发射在电视上做了实况转播。

senses.def: a horse, dog, etc. that has the particular chance of winning a race that is mentioned

ex.en: The horse is a 10–1 shot.
ex.cn: 这匹马的获胜率为 10:1。

senses.def: very quickly and without hesitating

ex.en: If I had the chance to go there, I'd go like a shot.
ex.cn: 要是我有机会去那儿，我会毫不犹豫就去的。

senses.def: something that you say or do as a warning to sb about what might happen if they do not change, etc.
senses.chn: （若不改变就会有某种后果的）警告

senses.def: something that gives sb/sth the help or encouragement they need
senses.chn: 鼓舞的力量；令人振奋的事情；强心针

senses.def: an important person
to be the person who controls a situation
a guess; sth you do without knowing what the result will be

ex.en: The figure he came up with was really just a shot in the dark.
ex.cn: 他得出的数字实际上只是瞎猜而已。

senses.def: an attempt or a guess that is not likely to be successful but is worth trying
senses.chn: 成功希望不大的尝试；把握不大的猜测；姑妄一猜

ex.en: It's a long shot, but it just might work.
ex.cn: 没有什么把握，但也许行得通。

senses.def: not nearly; not at all

ex.en: It's not over yet—not by a long chalk.
ex.cn: 这事还没有了结，还差得远呢。

senses.def: a final remark, especially an unkind one, that sb makes as they leave
senses.chn: 临去的放话（尤指不友善的）

senses.def: having another colour showing through or mixed with the main colour

ex.en: shot silk
ex.cn: 闪光绸

senses.def: in a very bad condition; destroyed
senses.chn: 破烂不堪；筋疲力尽；毁坏

ex.en: The brakes on this car are shot.
ex.cn: 这辆车上的刹车完全失灵了。

ex.en: I'm shot—I'm too old for this job.
ex.cn: 我一点力气都没有了，我这岁数干不动这活儿了。

ex.en: After the accident his nerves were shot to pieces.
ex.cn: 经历了那场事故，他的神经脆弱到了极点。

senses.def: to get rid of sb/sth so you no longer have the problems they cause
containing a lot of a particular colour, quality or feature
senses.chn: 布满，充满，富有（某种颜色、品质或特征）

ex.en: a voice shot through with emotion
ex.cn: 富有感情的声音

senses.def: a long gun that fires a lot of small metal bullets (called shot) and is used especially for shooting birds or animals
a wedding that has to take place quickly because the woman is pregnant
senses.chn: （因女方怀孕而仓促举行的）闪电式结婚

senses.def: a way of playing in which a player takes risks in order to win more points
a popular form of karate
senses.chn: 松涛馆（空手道的一个流派）

senses.def: containing a lot of a particular colour, quality or feature
senses.chn: 布满，充满，富有（某种颜色、品质或特征）

ex.en: a voice shot through with emotion
ex.cn: 富有感情的声音

senses.def: used to show what is right, appropriate, etc., especially when criticizing sb's actions

ex.en: You shouldn't drink and drive.
ex.cn: 你不该酒后驾车。

ex.en: He should have been more careful.
ex.cn: 他应当更小心点儿才是。

ex.en: A present for me? You shouldn't have!(= used to thank sb politely)
ex.cn: 给我的礼物？您太客气了！

senses.def: used for giving or asking for advice

ex.en: You should stop worrying about it.
ex.cn: 你该不用再为此事担忧了。

ex.en: Should I call him and apologize?
ex.cn: 我是不是应该打电话向他道歉？

ex.en: I should wait a little longer, if I were you.
ex.cn: 假如我是你的话，我会再等一会儿。

ex.en: 'She doesn't think she'll get a job.' 'She should worry, with all her qualifications (= she does not need to worry).'
ex.cn: “她担心找不到工作。” “她那么好的条件，还担心什么呀。”

ex.en: You should take the baby to the doctor's.
ex.cn: 你应该把这婴儿带去看看医生。

ex.en: I ought to give up smoking.
ex.cn: 我应该戒烟。

senses.def: used to say that you expect sth is true or will happen

ex.en: We should arrive before dark.
ex.cn: 我们天黑以前应该能赶到。

ex.en: I should have finished the book by Friday.
ex.cn: 到星期五我应该能读完那本书。

ex.en: The roads should be less crowded today.
ex.cn: 今天路上该不那么拥挤了吧。

senses.def: used to say that sth that was expected has not happened

ex.en: It should be snowing now, according to the weather forecast.
ex.cn: 按天气预报，现在该下雪才是。

ex.en: The bus should have arrived ten minutes ago.
ex.cn: 公共汽车十分钟以前就该到了。

senses.def: used after I or we instead of would for describing what you would do if sth else happened first
senses.chn: （与 I 或 we 连用代替 would，表示虚拟结果）就将

ex.en: If I were asked to work on Sundays, I should resign.
ex.cn: 要是叫我星期天加班，我就辞职不干了。

senses.def: used to refer to a possible event or situation

ex.en: If you should change your mind, do let me know.
ex.cn: 假如你改变主意的话，一定要告诉我。

ex.en: In case you should need any help, here's my number.
ex.cn: 万一你需要帮助的话，这是我的电话号码。

ex.en: Should anyone call (= if anyone calls), please tell them I'm busy.
ex.cn: 如果有人打电话来，请告诉他我正忙着。

senses.def: used as the past form of shall when reporting what sb has said
senses.chn: （在间接引语中用作 shall 的过去时）

ex.en: He asked me what time he should come. (= His words were: 'What time shall I come?')
ex.cn: 他问我他应该什么时候来。

ex.en: I said (that) I should be glad to help.
ex.cn: 我说我乐意帮忙。

senses.def: used after that when sth is suggested or arranged
senses.chn: （用于 that 引导的、表示建议或安排的从句中）

ex.en: She recommended that I should take some time off.
ex.cn: 她建议我应该休息一段时间。

ex.en: In order that training should be effective it must be planned systematically.
ex.cn: 为使培训有成效，必须有系统的计划。

ex.en: She recommended that I take some time off.
ex.cn: 她建议我应该休息一段时间。

ex.en: In order that training be effective…
ex.cn: 为使培训有成效…

senses.def: used after that after many adjectives that describe feelings
senses.chn: （用于许多表示感情的形容词后的 that 从句中）

ex.en: I'm anxious that we should allow plenty of time.
ex.cn: 我殷切希望我们能留出充裕的时间。

ex.en: I find it astonishing that he should be so rude to you.
ex.cn: 他竟然对你这样无礼，真叫我吃惊。

senses.def: used with I and we in polite requests
senses.chn: （与 I 和 we 连用，表示客气地请求）

ex.en: I should like to call my lawyer.
ex.cn: 我希望给我的律师打个电话。

ex.en: We should be grateful for your help.
ex.cn: 对您的帮助我们会非常感激。

senses.def: used with I and we to give opinions that you are not certain about
senses.chn: （与 I 和 we 连用，表示没有把握）

ex.en: I should imagine it will take about three hours.
ex.cn: 我想得用差不多三个小时吧。

ex.en: 'Is this enough food for everyone?' ' I should think so.'
ex.cn: “这些食物够所有人吃吗？” “我觉得够了吧。”

ex.en: 'Will it matter?' ' I shouldn't think so.'
ex.cn: “这有关系吗？” “我觉得没有吧。”

senses.def: used for expressing strong agreement

ex.en: 'I know it's expensive but it will last for years.' ' I should hope so too! '
ex.cn: “我知道价钱贵，但能用好多年。” “我也是这么想的！”

ex.en: 'Nobody will oppose it.' ' I should think not! '
ex.cn: “谁也不会反对的。” “我想也是！”

senses.def: used to refuse sth or to show that you are annoyed at a request; used to express surprise about an event or a situation

ex.en: Why should I help him? He's never done anything for me.
ex.cn: 我干吗要帮他呢？他从来没为我做过什么。

ex.en: How should I know where you've left your bag?
ex.cn: 我怎么知道你把包丢在哪儿了？

ex.en: I got on the bus and who should be sitting in front of me but Tony!
ex.cn: 我上了公共汽车，没想到坐在我前面的竟然是托尼！

senses.def: used to tell sb that sth would amuse or surprise them if they saw or experienced it
senses.chn: （表示假如对方看见或经历某事物，一定会感兴趣或吃惊）真该，真应当

ex.en: You should have seen her face when she found out!
ex.cn: 你真该看看她发现事情真相时脸上的表情！

ex.en: I said I'd (I would) be late.
ex.cn: 我说我要迟到了。

ex.en: He'd (he would) have liked to have been an actor.
ex.cn: 他本来想当演员。

ex.en: I'd (I would) really prefer tea.
ex.cn: 我倒是更喜欢喝茶。

ex.en: We should really go and visit them soon.
ex.cn: 我们的确应该马上去看看他们。

ex.en: You should have seen it!
ex.cn: 你应该看见的！

phrases.pattern: why, how, who, what ~ sb/sth do
phrases.filled: why, how, who, what should sb/sth do

senses.def: either of the two parts of the body between the top of each arm and the neck

ex.en: He slung the bag over his shoulder.
ex.cn: 他把包一甩，挎在肩上。

ex.en: She tapped him on the shoulder.
ex.cn: 她拍了拍他的肩膀。

ex.en: He looked back over his shoulder.
ex.cn: 他扭头朝后看。

ex.en: She shrugged her shoulders (= showing that she didn't know or care).
ex.cn: 她耸了耸肩。

ex.en: an off-the-shoulder dress
ex.cn: 露肩连衣裙

ex.en: He carried the child on his shoulders.
ex.cn: 他把孩子扛在肩上。

senses.def: having the type of shoulders mentioned

ex.en: broad-shouldered
ex.cn: 宽肩的

senses.def: the part of a piece of clothing that covers the shoulder

ex.en: a jacket with padded shoulders
ex.cn: 带垫肩的夹克

senses.def: meat from the top part of one of the front legs of an animal that has four legs
a part of sth, such as a bottle or mountain, that is shaped like a shoulder

ex.en: The village lay just around the shoulder of the hill.
ex.cn: 村子恰好坐落在山肩处。

senses.def: an area of ground at the side of a road where vehicles can stop in an emergency
senses.chn: 路肩（公路两侧供车辆紧急停靠的地带）

ex.en: No shoulder for next 5 miles.
ex.cn: 前方 5 英里之内没有路肩。

senses.def: to be anxious and have the feeling that sb is going to do sth unpleasant or harmful to you
if blame, guilt, etc. is on sb's shoulders, they must take responsibility for it
to start working very hard at a particular task
senses.chn: 着手大干起来；全力以赴

senses.def: used to describe a person who listens to your problems and gives you sympathy
physically close to sb
as one group that has the same aims, opinions, etc.
to be sensitive about sth that happened in the past and become easily offended if it is mentioned because you think that you were treated unfairly
senses.chn: （因受过委屈而变得）敏感，好生气

senses.def: to treat sb in an unfriendly way
to be much better than other people or things
senses.chn: 比其他人（或事物）好得多；出类拔萃；鹤立鸡群

senses.def: to be a sensible person
used to describe a young person who acts in a more sensible way than you would expect for a person of their age
to meet and spend time with a famous person, socially or as part of your job
if you say sth straight from the shoulder, you are being very honest and direct, even if what you are saying is critical
to accept the responsibility for sth

ex.en: to shoulder the responsibility/blame for sth
ex.cn: 对某事承担责任／过失

ex.en: women who shoulder the double burden of childcare and full-time work
ex.cn: 既抚养孩子又做全职工作、承担着双重负担的妇女

senses.def: to push forward with your shoulder in order to get somewhere

ex.en: He shouldered his way through the crowd and went after her.
ex.cn: 他侧身从人群中挤了过去，跟在她后面。

ex.en: She shouldered past a woman with a screaming baby.
ex.cn: 她从一个怀抱啼哭婴儿的女人身边挤了过去。

senses.def: to push sb/sth out of your way with your shoulder

ex.en: He shouldered the man aside.
ex.cn: 他一膀子把那男人撞到了一旁。

senses.def: to carry sth on your shoulder

ex.en: She shouldered her bag and set off home.
ex.cn: 她扛起包朝家走去。

example.en: He shouldered his way through the crowd and went after her.
example.cn: 他侧身从人群中挤了过去，跟在她后面。

example.en: She shouldered past a woman with a screaming baby.
example.cn: 她从一个怀抱啼哭婴儿的女人身边挤了过去。

senses.def: a bag, especially a handbag, that is carried over the shoulder with a long narrow piece of leather, etc.
either of the two large flat bones at the top of the back
as high as a person's shoulders

ex.en: a shoulder-high wall
ex.cn: 一堵齐肩高的墙

ex.en: They carried him shoulder-high through the crowd.
ex.cn: 他们把他抬在肩头，穿过人群。

senses.def: long enough to reach your shoulders
a small piece of thick cloth that is sewn into the shoulder of a dress, jacket, etc. to make a person's shoulders look bigger
a piece of hard plastic that people wear under their shirts to protect their shoulders when playing American football, ice hockey, etc.
senses.chn: （美式足球、冰球等运动衣内的）护肩

senses.def: a strip of cloth on a dress or other piece of clothing that goes over your shoulder from the front to the back
a long strip of cloth, leather, etc. that is attached to a bag so that you can carry it over your shoulder
the practice of watching a person who is getting money from a machine, filling out a form, etc., in order to find out their personal information
senses.chn: 肩窥（窥视他人从提款机取款、填表等以了解其个人信息的做法）

senses.def: to say sth in a loud voice; to speak loudly/angrily to sb

ex.en: Stop shouting and listen!
ex.cn: 别嚷了，听着！

ex.en: I shouted for help but nobody came.
ex.cn: 我大声呼救，但没人来。

ex.en: Then he started shouting and swearing at her.
ex.cn: 这时，他冲着她又叫又骂起来。

ex.en: She shouted at him to shut the gate.
ex.cn: 她大声吆喝他把大门关上。

ex.en: to shout abuse/encouragement/orders
ex.cn: 高声辱骂／鼓励／命令

ex.en: He shouted that he couldn't swim.
ex.cn: 他大叫他不会游泳。

senses.def: to make a loud noise

ex.en: She shouted out in pain when she tried to move her leg.
ex.cn: 她想动动腿，结果疼得大叫起来。

senses.def: to buy drinks or food for sb in a bar, restaurant, etc.
senses.chn: （在酒吧、餐厅等）请人喝饮料（或吃东西）

ex.en: I'll shout—what are you drinking?
ex.cn: 我请客，你想喝什么？

ex.en: Who's going to shout me a drink?
ex.cn: 谁要请我喝一杯？

senses.def: to shout so that sb who is speaking cannot be heard
senses.chn: 用喊叫声盖过某人的讲话

ex.en: The speaker was shouted down by a group of protesters.
ex.cn: 一群抗议者大叫大嚷，盖过了讲话人的声音。

senses.def: to say sth in a loud voice so that it can be clearly heard

ex.en: Don't shout out all the answers.
ex.cn: 别把所有的答案都大声说出来。

ex.en: 'I'm over here!' I shouted out.
ex.cn: “我在这边！” 我大声喊道。

senses.def: a loud cry of anger, fear, excitement, etc.
senses.chn: （愤怒、害怕、激动等的）呼喊，喊叫声

ex.en: angry shouts
ex.cn: 愤怒的叫喊

ex.en: a shout of anger
ex.cn: 一声怒吼

ex.en: I heard her warning shout too late.
ex.cn: 我听到她的大声警告，但已经太晚了。

senses.def: a person's turn to buy drinks

ex.en: What are you drinking? It's my shout.
ex.cn: 你喝什么？该我请客了。

senses.def: to have a good chance of winning sth or of achieving sth
to tell sb sth

ex.en: Give me a shout when you're ready.
ex.cn: 准备好了告诉我一声。

example.en: I shouted for help but nobody came.
example.cn: 我大声呼救，但没人来。

example.en: Then he started shouting and swearing at her.
example.cn: 这时，他冲着她又叫又骂起来。

phrases.filled: shout at sb to do sth

example.en: She shouted at him to shut the gate.
example.cn: 她大声吆喝他把大门关上。

example.en: to shout abuse/encouragement/orders
example.cn: 高声辱骂／鼓励／命令

example.en: He shouted that he couldn't swim.
example.cn: 他大叫他不会游泳。

example.en: She shouted herself hoarse, cheering on the team.
example.cn: 她为运动队加油，嗓子都喊哑了。

example.en: 'Run!' he shouted.
example.cn: “跑！” 他大喊一声。

example.en: Who's going to shout me a drink?
example.cn: 谁要请我喝一杯？

senses.def: loud cries from a number of people

ex.en: Didn't you hear all the shouting?
ex.cn: 你难道没有听到那一片叫喊声？

senses.def: to be almost finished or decided, so that there is no doubt about the final result
senses.chn: 基本大功告成；大局已定；胜负已分明

senses.def: very close
an argument or a disagreement when people shout loudly at each other
a public expression of thanks or welcome

ex.en: This is a shout-out to all our sponsors and advertisers.
ex.cn: 这是对我们所有赞助方和广告商的公开致谢。

senses.def: doing or involving a lot of shouting
senses.chn: 大喊大叫的；吵吵嚷嚷的

ex.en: a shouty conversation on the stairs
ex.cn: 楼梯上的高声谈话

senses.def: to push sb/sth in a rough way

ex.en: The crowd was pushing and shoving to get a better view.
ex.cn: 人们挤来挤去，想看得清楚点儿。

ex.en: The door wouldn't open no matter how hard she shoved.
ex.cn: 她怎么使劲推，门都推不开。

ex.en: He shoved her down the stairs.
ex.cn: 他把她推下楼梯。

senses.def: to put sth somewhere roughly or carelessly
senses.chn: 乱放；随便放；胡乱丢；随手扔

ex.en: She shoved the book into her bag and hurried off.
ex.cn: 她把书胡乱塞进包里就急急忙忙走了。

ex.en: He came over and shoved a piece of paper into my hand.
ex.cn: 他走过来往我手里塞了一张纸条。

ex.en: Shove your suitcase under the bed.
ex.cn: 把你的手提箱塞到床底下吧。

senses.def: used to say rudely that you will not accept or do sth
senses.chn: （粗鲁地表示不接受或不做某事）去他的，没门儿，去他妈的

ex.en: 'The boss wants that report now.' 'Yeah? Tell him he can shove it.'
ex.cn: “老板现在要那份报告。” “是吗？你告诉他没门儿。”

senses.def: used to tell sb rudely to go away
to move in order to make a space for sb to sit down beside you

ex.en: Shove up! Jan wants to sit down.
ex.cn: 挪一挪！简要坐下来。

senses.def: a strong push

ex.en: You have to give the door a shove or it won't close.
ex.cn: 这门你得猛推一下，否则关不上。

example.en: The door wouldn't open no matter how hard she shoved.
example.cn: 她怎么使劲推，门都推不开。

example.en: He shoved her down the stairs.
example.cn: 他把她推下楼梯。

senses.def: used to say rudely that you will not accept or do sth
senses.chn: （粗鲁地表示不接受或不做某事）去他的，没门儿，去他妈的

ex.en: 'The boss wants that report now.' 'Yeah? Tell him he can shove it.'
ex.cn: “老板现在要那份报告。” “是吗？你告诉他没门儿。”

senses.def: a tool with a long handle and a broad blade with curved edges, used for moving earth, snow, sand, etc.

ex.en: workmen with picks and shovels
ex.cn: 手拿镐铲的工人

ex.en: The children took their pails and shovels to the beach.
ex.cn: 孩子们带着桶和铲子到海滩上去了。

senses.def: the part of a large machine or vehicle that digs or moves earth
senses.chn: （推土机、挖土机等的）铲，铲形部分

senses.def: to lift and move earth, stones, coal, etc. with a shovel

ex.en: A gang of workmen were shovelling rubble onto a truck.
ex.cn: 一帮工人正用铁锹往卡车上装碎石。

ex.en: They went out in freezing conditions to shovel snow.
ex.cn: 他们冒着严寒出去铲雪。

ex.en: to shovel the sidewalk/driveway (= to remove snow)
ex.cn: 铲除人行道／车行道上的积雪

ex.en: He sat at the table, shovelling food into his mouth.
ex.cn: 他坐在桌前，一个劲地往嘴里塞吃的。

senses.def: the amount that a shovel can hold
(of a construction project) at the stage where workers can be employed and building begun
senses.chn: （建筑工程）准备就绪的，可马上动工的

senses.def: used to tell sb rudely to go away
to move in order to make a space for sb to sit down beside you

ex.en: Shove up! Jan wants to sit down.
ex.cn: 挪一挪！简要坐下来。

senses.def: to make sth clear; to prove sth

ex.en: The figures clearly show that her claims are false.
ex.cn: 这些数字清楚地表明，她的说法是错误的。

ex.en: Market research has shown us that people want quality, not just low prices.
ex.cn: 市场研究告诉我们，人们需要的是高质量，而不仅仅是低价格。

ex.en: a report showing the company's current situation
ex.cn: 表明公司当前状况的一份报告

ex.en: His new book shows him to be a first-rate storyteller.
ex.cn: 他的新著表明他讲故事的本领是一流的。

ex.en: This shows how people are influenced by TV advertisements.
ex.cn: 这表明电视广告对人们的影响有多大。

ex.en: This bar chart illustrates how many journeys people made on public transport over a three-month period.
ex.cn: 这个柱状图显示三个月期间人们乘坐公共交通往来的次数。

senses.def: to let sb see sth

ex.en: You have to show your ticket as you go in.
ex.cn: 进场必须出示门票。

ex.en: If there's a letter from France please show it to me.
ex.cn: 如有法国来的信，请拿给我看看。

ex.en: Have you shown your work to anyone?
ex.cn: 你有没有把你做的活儿给谁看过？

ex.en: Have you shown anyone your work?
ex.cn: 你有没有给谁看过你做的活儿？

senses.def: to help sb to do sth by letting them watch you do it or by explaining it

ex.en: She showed the technique to her students.
ex.cn: 她向学生演示了那个技巧。

ex.en: She showed her students the technique.
ex.cn: 她向学生演示了那个技巧。

ex.en: Can you show me how to do it?
ex.cn: 你能教我怎么做吗？

senses.def: to point to sth so that sb can see where or what it is

ex.en: He showed me our location on the map.
ex.cn: 他在地图上给我指出我们所处的位置。

ex.en: Show me which picture you drew.
ex.cn: 指给我看哪张画是你画的。

senses.def: to lead or guide sb to a place

ex.en: The attendant showed us to our seats.
ex.cn: 服务员把我们带到我们的座位。

ex.en: We were shown into the waiting room.
ex.cn: 我们被领进等候室。

ex.en: I'll go first and show you the way.
ex.cn: 我先走，给你带路。

ex.en: It's too far to walk—I'll take you by car.
ex.cn: 步行路太远，我开车送你去。

ex.en: Firefighters led the survivors to safety.
ex.cn: 消防队员把幸存者带到了安全的地方。

ex.en: The president arrived, escorted by twelve bodyguards.
ex.cn: 总统在十二名保镖的护送下到达。

senses.def: to make it clear that you have a particular quality

ex.en: to show great courage
ex.cn: 表现出极大的勇气

ex.en: She had shown herself unable to deal with money.
ex.cn: 她所做的事已表明她不善理财。

ex.en: He has shown himself to be ready to make compromises.
ex.cn: 他表现出自己愿意妥协。

ex.en: He has shown that he is ready to make compromises.
ex.cn: 他表现出愿意妥协。

senses.def: to behave in a particular way towards sb

ex.en: They showed no respect for their parents.
ex.cn: 他们毫不尊敬自己的父母。

ex.en: They showed their parents no respect.
ex.cn: 他们毫不尊敬自己的父母。

senses.def: if a feeling or quality shows, or if you show it, people can see it

ex.en: Fear showed in his eyes.
ex.cn: 他眼里显出了害怕的神色。

ex.en: She tried not to let her disappointment show.
ex.cn: 她极力掩饰自己的失望情绪。

ex.en: She's nearly forty now. And it shows (= it's obvious).
ex.cn: 她年近四十，一望便知。

ex.en: Her expression showed her disappointment.
ex.cn: 从她的表情可以看出她很失望。

ex.en: James began to show signs of impatience.
ex.cn: 詹姆斯开始显得不耐烦。

ex.en: She tried not to show how disappointed she was.
ex.cn: 她极力掩饰她是多么失望。

senses.def: if sth shows, people can see it. If sth shows a mark, dirt, etc., the mark can be seen.

ex.en: She had a warm woollen hat and scarf on that left only her eyes and nose showing.
ex.cn: 她戴着保暖呢帽和围巾，只露出了眼睛和鼻子。

ex.en: Their new white carpet showed every mark.
ex.cn: 他们新铺的白地毯有一点脏都看得出。

senses.def: to give particular information, or a time or measurement
senses.chn: 标示，表明（信息、时间、计量）

ex.en: The map shows the principal towns and rivers.
ex.cn: 这张地图标出了主要城镇和河流。

ex.en: The clock showed midnight.
ex.cn: 时钟显示已是午夜。

ex.en: The end-of-year accounts show a loss.
ex.cn: 年终账面显示出现了亏损。

senses.def: to be of sb/sth; to represent sb/sth

ex.en: She had objected to a photo showing her in a bikini.
ex.cn: 她曾反对给自己拍穿比基尼泳装的照片。

senses.def: to be or make sth available for the public to see

ex.en: The movie is now showing at all major movie theaters.
ex.cn: 这部影片目前正在各大影院上映。

ex.en: The movie is being shown now.
ex.cn: 这部影片目前正在上映。

ex.en: She plans to show her paintings early next year.
ex.cn: 她计划明年初展出自己的绘画作品。

senses.def: to prove that you can do sth or are sth

ex.en: They think I can't do it, but I'll show them!
ex.cn: 他们以为我做不了，我却要做给他们看看！

ex.en: He has shown himself to be a caring father.
ex.cn: 他已经证明了自己是个有爱心的父亲。

senses.def: to arrive where you have arranged to meet sb or do sth

ex.en: I waited an hour but he didn't show.
ex.cn: 我等了一个小时，可他一直没露面。

senses.def: to enter an animal in a competition
used to say that sth proves sth

ex.en: It just goes to show what you can do when you really try.
ex.cn: 这就表明，当你真下功夫时能做成什么事。

senses.def: to ask sb to leave, because they are no longer welcome
to appear among your friends or in public

ex.en: She stayed at home, afraid to show her face.
ex.cn: 她待在家里，不敢露面。

senses.def: to make your plans or intentions known
senses.chn: 摊牌；让对手摸着底细；公开自己的意图

senses.def: to make it clear to sb that you have more power and authority than they have
to do sth first so that other people can follow
to show that you are ready to help, work hard, etc. if necessary
senses.chn: 表示愿意；有乐于…的意思

senses.def: (to have) something, nothing, etc. as a result of sth
senses.chn: 在…方面有（或没有等）成绩；在…方面有（或没有等）结果

ex.en: All those years of hard work, and nothing to show for it!
ex.cn: 苦干这么多年，却毫无成绩可言！

senses.def: to show your support for your country, an organization or an idea to encourage or persuade others to do the same
senses.chn: 表示并号召拥护自己的国家（或某组织、某思想）

senses.def: to perform a particular activity in order to show other people what you are capable of doing
to show sb/know/learn how a particular job should be done
senses.chn: 向某人演示／知道／学会如何做某事

senses.def: to be a guide for sb when they visit a place for the first time to show them what is interesting
senses.chn: 领（某人）参观；带（某人）巡视

ex.en: We were shown around the school by one of the students.
ex.cn: 我们由其中一名学生领着参观了学校。

ex.en: Has anyone shown you round yet?
ex.cn: 有没有人带你四处走走？

senses.def: to try to impress others by talking about your abilities, possessions, etc.

ex.en: He's just showing off because that girl he likes is here.
ex.cn: 他不过是在表现自己，因为他喜欢的那个姑娘在场。

senses.def: to show people sb/sth that you are proud of

ex.en: She wanted to show off her new husband at the party.
