ex.cn: 我太累，径直上床睡了。

ex.en: She went straight from college to a top job.
ex.cn: 她大学一毕业就干上了一份优越的工作。

ex.en: I'm going to the library straight after the class.
ex.cn: 我一下课就马上去图书馆。

ex.en: I'll come straight to the point —your work isn't good enough.
ex.cn: 我开门见山地说吧，你的工作做得不够好。

senses.def: in or into a level or vertical position; in or into the correct position

ex.en: Sit up straight!
ex.cn: 坐直了！

ex.en: She pulled her hat straight.
ex.cn: 她把帽子拉正了。

senses.def: honestly and directly

ex.en: I told him straight that I didn't like him.
ex.cn: 我坦率地告诉他说我不喜欢他。

ex.en: Are you playing straight with me?
ex.cn: 你没跟我耍花招吧？

senses.def: continuously without interruption

ex.en: They had been working for 16 hours straight.
ex.cn: 他们已经一连工作了 16 个小时。

senses.def: to stop being a criminal and live an honest life
to be honest and not try to trick sb
immediately; without delay

ex.en: I'll do it straight away.
ex.cn: 这件事我马上就做。

senses.def: if you say sth straight from the shoulder, you are being very honest and direct, even if what you are saying is critical
without hesitating

ex.en: She asked him straight off what he thought about it all.
ex.cn: 她率直地问他对这一切有什么想法。

senses.def: used to ask if what sb has said is true or to emphasize that what you have said is true
senses.chn: （询问或强调所说的话的真实性）真的，确实

ex.en: I saw it—straight up!
ex.cn: 我亲眼看见了，真的！

senses.def: to be very obvious to sb
given by sb who is directly involved and therefore likely to be accurate
to think in a clear or logical way
without a bend or curve; going in one direction only

ex.en: a straight line
ex.cn: 直线

ex.en: a straight road
ex.cn: 笔直的公路

ex.en: long straight hair (= without curls)
ex.cn: 又长又直的头发

ex.en: a boat sailing in a straight line
ex.cn: 直线航行的船

ex.en: straight-backed chairs
ex.cn: 直背椅

senses.def: not fitting close to the body and not curving away from the body

ex.en: a straight skirt
ex.cn: 直筒裙

senses.def: going directly to the correct place

ex.en: a straight punch to the face
ex.cn: 不偏不倚打在脸上的一拳

senses.def: positioned in the correct way; level, vertical or parallel to sth
senses.chn: 平正的；正的；直的；与…平行的

ex.en: Is my tie straight?
ex.cn: 我的领带正不正？

senses.def: clean and neat, with everything in the correct place

ex.en: It took hours to get the house straight.
ex.cn: 用了好半天才把房子收拾出来。

senses.def: honest and direct

ex.en: a straight answer to a straight question
ex.cn: 问得直率，答得坦诚

ex.en: I don't think you're being straight with me.
ex.cn: 我觉得你没有跟我坦诚相见。

ex.en: It's time for some straight talking.
ex.cn: 现在该开诚布公地谈谈了。

ex.en: Thank you for being so honest with me.
ex.cn: 感谢你对我这么坦诚。

ex.en: To be frank with you, I think your son has little chance of passing the exam.
ex.cn: 坦白说，我认为你的儿子不大可能通过考试。

ex.en: You'll have to get used to his direct manner.
ex.cn: 你得慢慢习惯他这种直率的方式。

senses.def: simple; involving only two clear choices
senses.chn: 简单明了的；非此即彼的

ex.en: It was a straight choice between taking the job and staying out of work.
ex.cn: 要么接受这份工作，要么继续失业，此外别无其他选择。

ex.en: The election was a straight fight between the two main parties.
ex.cn: 那次选举是两大党直接交锋。

senses.def: not connected with comedy or musical theatre, but with serious theatre
senses.chn: 严肃的，正统的（与喜剧、音乐剧无关）

senses.def: one after another in a series, without interruption

ex.en: The team has had five straight wins.
ex.cn: 这支队已连赢五场比赛了。

senses.def: not mixed with water or anything else
senses.chn: 纯的；不掺水（或其他东西）的

senses.def: you can use straight to describe a person who is normal and ordinary, but who you consider dull and boring
senses.chn: 规矩老实的；本分无趣的；正统的

senses.def: heterosexual
to make a situation clear; to make sure that you or sb else understands the situation
senses.chn: 明确某事；把某事弄清楚

ex.en: Let's get this straight—you really had no idea where he was?
ex.cn: 我们把这个明确一下，你当时真的不知道他在哪儿？

senses.def: to correct sb's mistake; to make sure that sb knows the correct facts when they have had the wrong idea or impression
senses.chn: 纠正某人；指出某人的错误；使某人了解真相

senses.def: (to get) the best marks/grades in all your classes

ex.en: a straight A student
ex.cn: 全优生

senses.def: the honest and morally acceptable way of living

ex.en: His wife is trying to keep him on the straight and narrow.
ex.cn: 他妻子想方设法让他要诚实正派。

senses.def: if you keep a straight face, you do not laugh or smile, although you find sth funny
senses.chn: 绷着的脸；忍着不笑的脸

senses.def: with a very straight back and looking serious and formal
to give people the correct information about sth in order to make it clear that what they previously believed was in fact wrong
a person who has sexual relationships with people of the opposite sex, rather than the same sex

ex.en: gays and straights
ex.cn: 同性恋者和异性恋者

senses.def: a straight part of a racetrack or road
to push away a player who is trying to stop you, with your arm straight
a person who is very honest or who never does anything exciting or different
senses.chn: 老实巴交的人；循规蹈矩的人

senses.def: immediately; without delay

ex.en: I'll do it straight away.
ex.cn: 这件事我马上就做。

senses.def: a strip of wood, metal or plastic with a straight edge used for drawing accurate straight lines, or checking them
senses.chn: （用以画或测定直线的）直尺，标尺，规板

senses.def: to become straight; to make sth straight

ex.en: I straightened my tie and walked in.
ex.cn: 我把领带拉正，走了进去。

ex.en: The road bends here then straightens out.
ex.cn: 公路在这儿拐弯，然后就直了。

senses.def: to make your body straight and vertical

ex.en: He stood up and straightened his shoulders.
ex.cn: 他站起身，挺起肩膀。

ex.en: I straightened myself up to answer the question.
ex.cn: 我直起身来回答问题。

ex.en: Straighten up slowly, then repeat the exercise ten times.
ex.cn: 慢慢挺直身体，然后把这个动作重复十次。

senses.def: to help sb to deal with problems or understand a confused situation
senses.chn: 帮人解决问题；为人解除困惑

senses.def: to deal with a confused situation by organizing things that are causing problems

ex.en: I need time to straighten out my finances.
ex.cn: 我需要时间整理一下我的财务。

senses.def: to make sth neat and tidy

example.en: I straightened my tie and walked in.
example.cn: 我把领带拉正，走了进去。

example.en: The road bends here then straightens out.
example.cn: 公路在这儿拐弯，然后就直了。

example.en: He stood up and straightened his shoulders.
example.cn: 他站起身，挺起肩膀。

example.en: I straightened myself up to answer the question.
example.cn: 我直起身来回答问题。

example.en: Straighten up slowly, then repeat the exercise ten times.
example.cn: 慢慢挺直身体，然后把这个动作重复十次。

senses.def: any substance that you can use to make your hair straight

ex.en: chemical straighteners
ex.cn: 化学直发剂

senses.def: without laughing or smiling, even though you may be amused
easy to do or to understand; not complicated
senses.chn: 简单的；易懂的；不复杂的

ex.en: a straightforward process
ex.cn: 简单的过程

ex.en: It's quite straightforward to get here.
ex.cn: 来这儿相当容易。

senses.def: honest and open; not trying to trick sb or hide sth
if you say sth straight from the shoulder, you are being very honest and direct, even if what you are saying is critical
a person in a show whose role is to provide the main entertainer with opportunities to make jokes
(in elections in the US) a vote in which sb chooses all the candidates from the same party
senses.chn: 清一色选票（美国选举中支持同一政党全部候选人的选票）

senses.def: used to ask if what sb has said is true or to emphasize that what you have said is true
senses.chn: （询问或强调所说的话的真实性）真的，确实

ex.en: I saw it—straight up!
ex.cn: 我亲眼看见了，真的！

senses.def: pressure on sb/sth because they have too much to do or manage, or sth very difficult to deal with; the problems, worry or anxiety that this produces
senses.chn: 压力；重负；重压之下出现的问题（或担忧等）

ex.en: Their marriage is under great strain at the moment.
ex.cn: 眼下他们的婚姻关系非常紧张。

ex.en: These repayments are putting a strain on our finances.
ex.cn: 偿还这些债务对我们的财务状况形成了压力。

ex.en: Relax, and let us take the strain (= do things for you).
ex.cn: 你歇一下，我们来顶一会儿。

ex.en: The transport service cannot cope with the strain of so many additional passengers.
ex.cn: 运输部门无法应对增加这么多乘客所带来的紧张局面。

ex.en: You will learn to cope with the stresses and strains of public life.
ex.cn: 你要学会应付公众人物生活的紧张和辛劳。

ex.en: I found it a strain having to concentrate for so long.
ex.cn: 我觉得这么长时间全神贯注挺累的。

senses.def: the pressure that is put on sth when a physical force stretches, pushes, or pulls it

ex.en: The rope broke under the strain.
ex.cn: 绳子给拉断了。

ex.en: You should try not to place too much strain on muscles and joints.
ex.cn: 你要尽量不让肌肉和关节太吃力。

ex.en: The ground here cannot take the strain of a large building.
ex.cn: 这块地承受不住大型建筑的压力。

ex.en: The cable has a 140kg breaking strain (= it will break when it is stretched or pulled by a force greater than this).
ex.cn: 这种缆索的断裂应变力为 140 千克。

senses.def: an injury to a part of your body, such as a muscle, that is caused by using it too much or by twisting it

ex.en: a calf/groin/leg strain
ex.cn: 腿肚子／腹股沟／腿部拉伤

ex.en: muscle strain
ex.cn: 肌肉劳损

senses.def: a particular type of plant or animal, or of a disease caused by bacteria, etc.
senses.chn: （动、植物的）系，品系，品种；（疾病的）类型

ex.en: a new strain of mosquitoes resistant to the poison
ex.cn: 对这种毒药有抗药性的新品种蚊子

ex.en: This is only one of the many strains of the disease.
ex.cn: 这种病有许多类型，这只是其中之一。

senses.def: a particular tendency in the character of a person or group, or a quality in their manner
senses.chn: 个性特点；性格倾向；禀性

ex.en: He had a definite strain of snobbery in him.
ex.cn: 他这个人明显有一股势利小人的气味。

senses.def: the sound of music being played or sung

ex.en: She could hear the strains of Mozart through the window.
ex.cn: 她听见从窗户飘出的莫扎特的旋律。

senses.def: to injure yourself or part of your body by making it work too hard

ex.en: to strain a muscle
ex.cn: 拉伤肌肉

ex.en: He injured his knee playing hockey.
ex.cn: 他打曲棍球时膝盖受了伤。

ex.en: Three people were injured in the crash.
ex.cn: 撞车事故中有三人受伤。

ex.en: 50 people were seriously wounded in the attack.
ex.cn: 这次攻击中有 50 人受重伤。

ex.en: Did you hurt yourself?
ex.cn: 你伤着自己了吗？

ex.en: Don't strain your eyes by reading in poor light.
ex.cn: 别在光线不足的地方看书把眼睛给伤了。

senses.def: to make an effort to do sth, using all your mental or physical strength

ex.en: I strained my ears (= listened very hard) to catch what they were saying.
ex.cn: 我竖起耳朵去听他们在说些什么。

ex.en: Necks were strained for a glimpse of the stranger.
ex.cn: 大家伸长了脖子想看一看这个陌生人。

ex.en: People were straining to see what was going on.
ex.cn: 人们翘首企足看发生了什么事。

ex.en: He burst to the surface, straining for air.
ex.cn: 他冲出水面，使劲吸气。

ex.en: Bend gently to the left without straining.
ex.cn: 轻轻向左弯，不要用力。

senses.def: to try to make sth do more than it is able to do

ex.en: The sudden influx of visitors is straining hotels in the town to the limit.
ex.cn: 游客突然涌入，城里的旅馆全都爆满。

ex.en: His constant complaints were straining our patience.
ex.cn: 他没完没了的抱怨让我们忍无可忍。

ex.en: The dispute has strained relations between the two countries (= made them difficult).
ex.cn: 这场争端使两国关系紧张起来。

senses.def: to push hard against sth; to pull hard on sth

ex.en: She strained against the ropes that held her.
ex.cn: 她使劲挣了挣拴着她的绳子。

ex.en: The dogs were straining at the leash, eager to get to the park.
ex.cn: 几条狗用力拽着皮带，急于要去公园。

senses.def: to pour food, etc. through sth with very small holes in it, for example a sieve, in order to separate the solid part from the liquid part

ex.en: Use a colander to strain the vegetables.
ex.cn: 把蔬菜放在漏筐里控控水。

ex.en: Strain off any excess liquid.
ex.cn: 滤掉多余的液体。

senses.def: to want to do sth very much

ex.en: Like all youngsters, he's straining at the leash to leave home.
ex.cn: 跟所有年轻人一样，他也急于离开家生活。

senses.def: to try as hard as you can to do sth
if a system or service creaks under the strain, it cannot deal effectively with all the things it is expected to do or provide
senses.chn: 因负担过重而效率低下；由于压力过大而运转不灵

example.en: I strained my ears (= listened very hard) to catch what they were saying.
example.cn: 我竖起耳朵去听他们在说些什么。

example.en: Necks were strained for a glimpse of the stranger.
example.cn: 大家伸长了脖子想看一看这个陌生人。

example.en: People were straining to see what was going on.
example.cn: 人们翘首企足看发生了什么事。

example.en: He burst to the surface, straining for air.
example.cn: 他冲出水面，使劲吸气。

example.en: Strain off any excess liquid.
example.cn: 滤掉多余的液体。

senses.def: to want to do sth very much

ex.en: Like all youngsters, he's straining at the leash to leave home.
ex.cn: 跟所有年轻人一样，他也急于离开家生活。

senses.def: showing the effects of worry or pressure
senses.chn: 神色不宁的；紧张的；憔悴的

ex.en: Her face looked strained and weary.
ex.cn: 她的脸色显得憔悴疲惫。

ex.en: He spoke in a low, strained voice.
ex.cn: 他焦虑地低声说话。

senses.def: not relaxed or friendly

ex.en: There was a strained atmosphere throughout the meeting.
ex.cn: 会议自始至终气氛紧张。

ex.en: Relations between the two families are strained.
ex.cn: 两家关系紧张。

senses.def: not natural; produced by a deliberate effort
senses.chn: 不自然的；做作的；勉强的

ex.en: She gave a strained laugh.
ex.cn: 她不自然地大笑了一声。

senses.def: a kitchen utensil (= a tool) with a lot of small holes in it, used for separating solids from liquids

ex.en: a tea-strainer
ex.cn: 滤茶器

senses.def: a narrow passage of water that connects two seas or large areas of water
senses.chn: 海峡；（连结两大水域的）水道

ex.en: the Strait(s) of Gibraltar
ex.cn: 直布罗陀海峡

senses.def: a very difficult situation especially because of lack of money
senses.chn: （尤指经济拮据引起的）困境，境况窘迫

ex.en: The factory is in dire straits.
ex.cn: 工厂岌岌可危。

ex.en: She found herself in desperate financial straits.
ex.cn: 她发觉自己经济状况极为窘迫。

senses.def: without enough money or as much money as there was before
senses.chn: 经济拮据的；穷困的；经济状况恶化的

ex.en: The family of eight was living in straitened circumstances.
ex.cn: 这个八口之家日子过得很拮据。

senses.def: a piece of clothing like a jacket with long arms which are tied to prevent the person wearing it from behaving violently. Straitjackets are sometimes used to control people who are mentally ill.
senses.chn: 约束衣，紧身衣（有时用以束缚精神病患者）

senses.def: a thing that stops sth from growing or developing

ex.en: the straitjacket of taxation
ex.cn: 纳税的束缚

senses.def: having strict or old-fashioned ideas about people's moral behaviour
senses.chn: （在道德行为上）拘谨保守的，古板的

senses.def: a single thin piece of thread, wire, hair, etc.

ex.en: a strand of wool
ex.cn: 一股羊毛

ex.en: a few strands of dark hair
ex.cn: 几绺黑发

ex.en: She wore a single strand of pearls around her neck.
ex.cn: 她脖子上戴着单串珍珠。

senses.def: one of the different parts of an idea, a plan, a story, etc.
senses.chn: （观点、计划、故事等的）部分，方面

ex.en: We heard every strand of political opinion.
ex.cn: 各派的政治观点我们都听到了。

ex.en: The author draws the different strands of the plot together in the final chapter.
ex.cn: 作者在最后一章把不同的情节线索归拢到了一起。

senses.def: the land along the edge of the sea or ocean, or of a lake or river
to leave sb in a place from which they have no way of leaving

ex.en: The strike left hundreds of tourists stranded at the airport.
ex.cn: 这场罢工使成百上千的游客滞留在机场。

senses.def: to make a boat, fish, whale, etc. be left on land and unable to return to the water

ex.en: The ship was stranded on a sandbank.
ex.cn: 船在沙洲上搁浅了。

senses.def: unusual or surprising, especially in a way that is difficult to understand

ex.en: A strange thing happened this morning.
ex.cn: 今天上午发生了一件怪事。

ex.en: She was looking at me in a very strange way.
ex.cn: 她用十分异样的目光看着我。

ex.en: It's strange (that) we haven't heard from him.
ex.cn: 奇怪，我们一直没有他的消息。

ex.en: It's strange how childhood impressions linger.
ex.cn: 童年的印象经久不忘，真是不可思议。

ex.en: That's strange —the front door's open.
ex.cn: 怪事，正门开着。

ex.en: I'm looking forward to the exam, strange as it may seem.
ex.cn: 别人可能感到奇怪，我在盼望这场考试。

senses.def: not familiar because you have not been there before or met the person before

ex.en: a strange city
ex.cn: 陌生的城市

ex.en: to wake up in a strange bed
ex.cn: 在陌生的床上醒来

ex.en: Never accept lifts from strange men.
ex.cn: 千万别搭陌生男人的车。

ex.en: At first the place was strange to me.
ex.cn: 起先我对这个地方不熟悉。

senses.def: to not feel comfortable in a situation; to have an unpleasant physical feeling
senses.chn: 感觉不自在；感觉不舒服

ex.en: She felt strange sitting at her father's desk.
ex.cn: 坐在父亲的书桌前，她感觉不自在。

ex.en: It was terribly hot and I started to feel strange.
ex.cn: 酷热难当，我逐渐感到不舒服。

senses.def: used to say that things that actually happen are often more surprising than stories that are invented
senses.chn: 现实比虚构更不可思议

example.en: It's strange (that) we haven't heard from him.
example.cn: 奇怪，我们一直没有他的消息。

example.en: It's strange how childhood impressions linger.
example.cn: 童年的印象经久不忘，真是不可思议。

example.en: At first the place was strange to me.
example.cn: 起先我对这个地方不熟悉。

senses.def: in an unusual or surprising way
senses.chn: 异常地；奇怪地；不可思议地

ex.en: She's been acting very strangely lately.
ex.cn: 近来她举止十分反常。

ex.en: The house was strangely quiet.
ex.cn: 房子里静得出奇。

ex.en: strangely shaped rocks
ex.cn: 奇形怪状的岩石

ex.en: Strangely enough, I don't feel at all nervous.
ex.cn: 真奇怪，我一点也不紧张。

senses.def: a person that you do not know

ex.en: There was a complete stranger sitting at my desk.
ex.cn: 我书桌前坐着一个从未见过的陌生人。

ex.en: They got on well together although they were total strangers.
ex.cn: 尽管以前素未谋面，但他们相处融洽。

ex.en: We've told our daughter not to speak to strangers.
ex.cn: 我们告诉女儿不要和陌生人讲话。

ex.en: She remained a stranger to me.
ex.cn: 我一直未能了解她。

senses.def: a person who is in a place that they have not been in before

ex.en: Sorry, I don't know where the bank is. I'm a stranger here myself.
ex.cn: 对不起，我不知道银行在哪儿。我不是本地人。

ex.en: He must have been a stranger to the town.
ex.cn: 他当时一定是刚到这个镇子。

senses.def: to be familiar/not familiar with sth because you have/have not experienced it many times before
senses.chn: 熟悉（或不熟悉）某事；习惯（或不习惯）某事

ex.en: He is no stranger to controversy.
ex.cn: 他对争论见得多了。

example.en: She remained a stranger to me.
example.cn: 我一直未能了解她。

example.en: He must have been a stranger to the town.
example.cn: 他当时一定是刚到这个镇子。

senses.def: to kill sb by squeezing or pressing on their throat and neck

ex.en: to strangle sb to death
ex.cn: 把某人掐死

ex.en: He strangled her with her own scarf.
ex.cn: 他用她自己的围巾把她勒死了。

senses.def: to prevent sth from growing or developing

ex.en: The current monetary policy is strangling the economy.

ex.en: She has no intention of giving you a divorce; she's just stringing you along.
ex.cn: 她无意跟你离婚，不过是骗着你玩的。

senses.def: a man's vest made from a type of cloth with a regular pattern of large holes

senses.chn: 细长而干枯的；细长而稀疏的

senses.def: containing long thin pieces like string and difficult to chew

ex.cn: 又老筋又多的肉

senses.def: thin so that you can see the muscles

senses.def: to take off all or most of your clothes or another person's clothes
senses.chn: 脱光衣服；脱掉大部分衣服；扒光…的衣服

ex.en: I stripped and washed myself all over.
ex.cn: 我脱掉衣服，把全身洗了洗。

ex.en: She stripped down to her underwear.
ex.cn: 她把衣服脱得只剩下了内衣。

ex.en: We stripped off and ran down to the water.
ex.cn: 我们脱掉衣服，跑进水里。

ex.en: He stood there stripped to the waist (= he had no clothes on the upper part of his body).
ex.cn: 他脱光了上衣站在那里。

ex.en: He was stripped naked and left in a cell.
ex.cn: 他被扒得一丝不挂，丢在一间牢房里。

senses.def: to take off your clothes as a form of entertainment; to perform a striptease
senses.chn: 进行脱衣表演；表演脱衣舞

senses.def: to remove a layer from sth, especially so that it is completely exposed
senses.chn: 除去，剥去（一层）；（尤指）剥光

ex.en: Strip off all the existing paint.
ex.cn: 把现有的油漆全部刮掉。

ex.en: After the guests had gone, I stripped all the beds (= removed all the sheets in order to wash them).
ex.cn: 客人走后，我把被单床单全都撤了下来。

ex.en: Deer had stripped all the bark off the tree.
ex.cn: 鹿把树皮全都啃光了。

ex.en: Deer had stripped the tree of its bark.
ex.cn: 鹿啃掉了树皮。

senses.def: to remove all the things from a place and leave it empty
senses.chn: 从（某处）拿走所有东西；使（某处）空无一物

ex.en: We had to strip out all the old wiring and start again.
ex.cn: 我们不得不将原有的线路全部拆除，从头再来。

ex.en: Thieves had stripped the house bare.
ex.cn: 窃贼把房子洗劫一空。

senses.def: to separate a machine, etc. into parts so that they can be cleaned or repaired

ex.en: They taught us how to strip down a car engine and put it back together again.
ex.cn: 他们教我们拆卸、安装汽车引擎。

senses.def: to take away property or honours from sb, as a punishment

ex.en: He was disgraced and stripped of his title.
ex.cn: 他名誉扫地，被取消了头衔。

senses.def: to remove a layer from sth

ex.en: First, you need to strip away all the old plaster.
ex.cn: 首先，你得把原来的灰泥全部刮掉。

senses.def: to remove anything that is not true or necessary
senses.chn: 揭去，揭穿，清除（虚假或不必要的东西）

ex.en: The movie aims to strip away the lies surrounding Kennedy's life.
ex.cn: 这部电影旨在揭穿有关肯尼迪生平的种种谎言。

senses.def: a long narrow piece of paper, metal, cloth, etc.

ex.en: a strip of material
ex.cn: 一块布条

ex.en: Cut the meat into strips.
ex.cn: 把肉切成条。

senses.def: a long narrow area of land, sea, etc.
senses.chn: （陆地、海域等）狭长地带；带状水域

ex.cn: 加沙地带

ex.cn: 岛屿之间一衣带水。

senses.def: the uniform that is worn by the members of a sports team when they are playing

ex.cn: 身穿他们闻名遐迩的黑白条队服的尤文图斯队

ex.en: the team's away strip (= that they use when playing games away from home)

ex.cn: 形形色色的政界人士

ex.cn: 持各种政治观点的评论员

ex.cn: 她完全是另外一种类型的教育家。

senses.def: an act of hitting a ball, for example with a bat or racket

ex.en: What a beautiful stroke!
ex.cn: 击球动作多漂亮呀！

ex.en: He won by two strokes (= in golf, by taking two fewer strokes than his opponent).
ex.cn: 他以少于对手两杆的成绩获胜。

senses.def: a single movement of the arm when hitting sb/sth

ex.en: His punishment was six strokes of the cane.
ex.cn: 给他的惩罚是挨六教鞭。

senses.def: any of a series of repeated movements in swimming or rowing

ex.en: She took a few more strokes to reach the bank.
ex.cn: 她又划几下，游到了岸边。

senses.def: a style of swimming

ex.en: Butterfly is the only stroke I can't do.
ex.cn: 只有蝶泳我不会。

senses.def: the person who sets the speed at which everyone in a boat rows
senses.chn: （指挥船上其他桨手的）尾桨手

senses.def: an act of moving your hand gently over a surface, usually several times

ex.en: He gave the cat a stroke.
ex.cn: 他抚摩了一下猫。

senses.def: a mark made by moving a pen, brush, etc. once across a surface

ex.en: to paint with fine brush strokes
ex.cn: 一小刷一小刷地刷漆

ex.en: At the stroke of a pen (= by signing sth) they removed thousands of people from the welfare system.
ex.cn: 他们大笔一挥，就把成千上万的人排除在福利制度之外。

senses.chn: （成功的）举动；（高明的）举措；（巧妙的）办法；（成功的）事情

ex.en: Your idea was a stroke of genius.
ex.cn: 你的主意很高明。

ex.en: It was a stroke of luck that I found you here.
ex.cn: 我在这儿看见你纯属巧遇。

ex.en: It was a bold stroke to reveal the identity of the murderer on the first page.
ex.cn: 在头版上披露谋杀犯的身份，这是一个大胆的举措。

ex.en: She never does a stroke (of work) (= never does any work).
ex.cn: 她一向什么活儿都不干。

senses.def: each of the sounds made by a clock or bell giving the hours

ex.en: At the first stroke it will be 9 o'clock exactly.
ex.cn: 等到钟敲第一下时就是 9 点整。

ex.en: on the stroke of three (= at 3 o'clock exactly)
ex.cn: 三点整

senses.def: a sudden serious illness when a blood vessel (= tube) in the brain bursts or is blocked, which can cause death or the loss of the ability to move or to speak clearly

ex.en: to have/suffer a stroke
ex.cn: 患中风

ex.en: The stroke left him partly paralysed.
ex.cn: 他因中风身体局部瘫痪了。

senses.def: with a single immediate action

ex.en: They threatened to cancel the whole project at a stroke.
ex.cn: 他们威胁要一下子砍掉整个项目。

senses.def: to make sb make a mistake or hesitate in what they are doing
senses.chn: 扰乱某人；使某人乱了方寸

senses.def: to move your hand gently and slowly over an animal's fur or hair

ex.en: He's a beautiful dog. Can I stroke him?
ex.cn: 这只狗真漂亮，我可以摸一摸吗？

senses.def: to move your hand gently over a surface, sb's hair, etc.
senses.chn: 轻抚，抚摩（物体表面或头发等）

ex.en: He stroked her hair affectionately.
ex.cn: 他深情地抚摩着她的头发。

senses.def: to move sth somewhere with a gentle movement

ex.en: She stroked away his tears.
ex.cn: 她轻轻拭去他的眼泪。

ex.en: He stroked the ball between the posts.
ex.cn: 他轻轻一触，把球踢进门柱之间。

senses.def: to be very nice to sb, especially to get them to do what you want
senses.chn: 待（某人）非常好；（尤指）顺着（某人）以便为自己办事

to walk somewhere in a slow relaxed way

ex.en: People were strolling along the beach.
ex.cn: 人们在海滩漫步。

senses.def: a slow relaxed walk

ex.en: We went for a stroll in the park.
ex.cn: 我们去公园散了散步。

senses.def: a person who is enjoying a slow relaxed walk
a small folding seat on wheels in which a small child sits and is pushed along
having a lot of physical power so that you can lift heavy weights, do hard physical work, etc.

ex.en: strong muscles
ex.cn: 强健的肌肉

ex.en: She wasn't a strong swimmer (= she could not swim well).
ex.cn: 她游泳不大行。

ex.en: He's strong enough to lift a car!
ex.cn: 他力气大得能抬起一辆汽车！

senses.def: having great power

ex.en: Stay indoors in the middle of the day, when the sun is strongest.
ex.cn: 中午阳光最强的时候待在室内。

ex.en: a strong wind/current
ex.cn: 强风；急流

ex.en: a strong magnet
ex.cn: 强磁铁

senses.def: having a powerful effect on the body or mind

ex.en: a strong drug
ex.cn: 强效药物

senses.def: having a lot of power or influence
senses.chn: 有权势的；有影响的；有实力的

ex.en: a strong leader/government
ex.cn: 重权在握的领导人；强有力的政府

senses.def: people who are rich or powerful
senses.chn: 有钱人；有势者；强势群体

senses.def: very powerful and difficult for people to fight against or defeat

ex.en: a strong team
ex.cn: 强队

ex.en: The temptation to tell her everything was very strong.
ex.cn: 非常想把一切全都告诉她。

senses.def: difficult to attack or criticize

ex.en: There is strong evidence of a link between exercise and a healthy heart.
ex.cn: 有充分的证据证明锻炼有益于心脏健康。

ex.en: You have a strong case for getting your job back.
ex.cn: 你有充分的理由要求复职。

senses.def: holding an opinion or a belief very firmly and seriously
senses.chn: 坚决的；坚定的；不动摇的；始终不渝的

ex.en: a strong supporter/opponent of the government
ex.cn: 坚决拥护／反对政府的人

senses.def: very powerful

ex.en: strong support for the government
ex.cn: 对政府的坚决拥护

ex.en: People have strong feelings about this issue.
ex.cn: 人们对这个问题反应强烈。

senses.def: not easily broken or damaged; made well

ex.en: a strong chair
ex.cn: 结实的椅子

senses.def: not easily upset or frightened; not easily influenced by other people
senses.chn: 坚强的；不易受惊吓的；有主见的

ex.en: You need strong nerves to ride a bike in London.
ex.cn: 在伦敦骑自行车，你可得有胆量。

ex.en: It's difficult, I know. But be strong!
ex.cn: 我知道这不容易。不过要坚强！

ex.en: a strong personality
ex.cn: 坚强的个性

senses.def: likely to succeed or happen
senses.chn: 有望成功的；可能性大的

ex.en: a strong candidate for the job
ex.cn: 有望获得这份工作的人选

ex.en: You're in a strong position to negotiate a deal.
ex.cn: 你们很有希望通过谈判达成协议。

ex.en: There's a strong possibility that we'll lose the game.
ex.cn: 我们很有可能会输掉比赛。

senses.def: good at sth

ex.en: The play has a very strong cast.
ex.cn: 这部剧演员阵容强大。

ex.en: Mathematics was never my strong point (= I was never very good at it).
ex.cn: 数学从来不是我的强项。

senses.def: great in number

ex.en: There was a strong police presence at the demonstration.
ex.cn: 示威现场有大批警察。

senses.def: used after numbers to show the size of a group
senses.chn: （用于数字后，表示某集体的规模）多达…的，计有…的

ex.en: a 5 000-strong crowd
ex.cn: 多达 5 000 人的群众

ex.en: The crowd was 5 000 strong.
ex.cn: 聚集的人群有 5 000 人。

senses.def: not easily affected by disease; healthy
senses.chn: 健康的；强壮的；身体好的

ex.en: Are you feeling stronger now after your rest?
ex.cn: 休息过后，你是不是感觉好些了？

ex.en: I'm not feeling very well.
ex.cn: 我感觉身体不太好。

ex.en: Is he well enough to travel?
ex.cn: 他身体怎么样，能够旅行吗？

ex.en: Are you feeling all right?
ex.cn: 你感觉还好吗？

ex.en: She says she's OK now, and will be back at work tomorrow.
ex.cn: 她说她现在身体还可以，明天就回来上班。

ex.en: 'How are you?' 'Fine, thanks.'
ex.cn: “你好吗？” “很好，谢谢。”

senses.def: firmly established; difficult to destroy

ex.en: a strong marriage
ex.cn: 巩固的婚姻

ex.en: The college has strong links with local industry.
ex.cn: 这所学院同当地产业界有牢固的联系。

senses.def: having a value that is high or increasing
senses.chn: 坚挺的；行情看涨的；呈强势的

ex.en: strong share prices
ex.cn: 行情看涨的股票价格

ex.en: The euro is getting stronger against the dollar.
ex.cn: 欧元对美元呈强势走向。

senses.def: in a safe financial position
senses.chn: 经营状况良好的；景气的

ex.en: Their catering business remained strong despite the recession.
ex.cn: 尽管出现经济衰退，他们的酒席承办生意仍然景气。

senses.def: easy to see, hear, feel or smell; very great or intense
senses.chn: 醒目的；响亮的；明显感觉得到的；浓烈的；强烈的

ex.en: a strong smell
ex.cn: 浓烈的气味

ex.en: a strong feeling of nausea
ex.cn: 强烈的恶心感觉

ex.en: a strong voice (= loud)
ex.cn: 洪亮的嗓音

ex.en: strong colours
ex.cn: 浓重的色彩

ex.en: a face with strong features (= large and noticeable)
ex.cn: 轮廓分明的面孔

ex.en: She spoke with a strong Australian accent.
ex.cn: 她说话带有浓重的澳大利亚口音。

senses.def: having a lot of flavour

ex.en: strong cheese
ex.cn: 味重的奶酪

senses.def: containing a lot of a substance

ex.en: strong black coffee
ex.cn: 不加牛奶的浓咖啡

senses.def: having a lot of force, often causing offence to people

ex.en: The movie has been criticized for strong language (= swearing).
ex.cn: 这部电影因有脏话而受到批评。

senses.def: forming the past tense and past participle by changing a vowel, not by adding a regular ending, for example sing, sang, sung
senses.chn: 强变化的（通过改变元音而不是加规则的词尾来构成动词过去式和过去分词，如 sing、sang、sung）

senses.def: used to describe the way some words are pronounced when they have stress. For example, the strong form of and is /ænd/ .
senses.chn: 强读式的，重读的（某些词重读时的读音，如 and 的强式读音为 /ænd/ ）

senses.def: used to say that you think what sb has said is unfair or too critical
senses.chn: （认为某人的话有失公允或过于苛刻时说）有点言重了

senses.def: to be good at sth

ex.en: I'm not very strong on dates (= I can't remember the dates of important events).
ex.cn: 我不大记得住日期。

senses.def: to have a lot of sth
senses.chn: 某事物有很多；强于某一方面

ex.en: The report was strong on criticism, but short on practical suggestions.
ex.cn: 这份报告批评的话说得多，但可行的建议提得少。

senses.def: to be a subject that sb knows a lot about

ex.en: I'm afraid geography is not my strong suit.
ex.cn: 恐怕地理不是我的强项。

senses.def: to make your feelings clear in an aggressive way, especially your sexual feelings towards sb
senses.chn: 言行过分；（尤指）露骨地调情

senses.def: to continue to be healthy, active or successful
senses.chn: 保持健康；活跃依旧；兴盛不衰

ex.en: My grandmother is 90 and still going strong.
ex.cn: 我奶奶 90 岁了，还挺硬朗。

senses.def: to be able to see or do unpleasant things without feeling sick or upset
something that gives sb an advantage over other people in a particular situation
senses.chn: 某人的王牌；最强有力的一招；制胜的绝招

senses.def: using threats or violence in order to make people do what you want
senses.chn: 横施淫威的；以暴力强制的

ex.en: to use strong-arm tactics against your political opponents
ex.cn: 用强制手段对付政敌

senses.def: a strong, usually metal, box for keeping valuable things in
one of the four fundamental forces in the universe, which holds the parts of the nucleus of an atom together
senses.chn: 强力（宇宙四种基本力之一，将原子核各部分结合在一起）

senses.def: an area in which there is a lot of support for a particular belief or group of people, especially a political party
senses.chn: 有广泛支持的地方；势力强大的地方

ex.en: a Republican stronghold/a stronghold of Republicanism
ex.cn: 共和党势力强大的地区

senses.def: a castle or a place that is strongly built and difficult to attack
an area where there are a large number of a particular type of animal

ex.en: This valley is one of the last strongholds of the Siberian tiger.
ex.cn: 这条山谷是西伯利亚虎最后的几个主要栖息地之一。

ex.cn: 这部电影我没看过，不过人们普遍认为很不错。

ex.en: Of the six people injured in the crash, only two survived.
ex.cn: 因这次撞车事故受伤的六人中，只有两人活了下来。

ex.en: 'How are you these days?' 'Oh, surviving.'
ex.cn: “你近来好吗？” “嗐，凑合过吧。”

ex.en: Don't worry, it's only a scratch—you'll survive.
ex.cn: 别担心，只不过是划伤，你没事的。

ex.en: Some strange customs have survived from earlier times.
ex.cn: 有些奇怪的风俗是从早年留存下来的。

ex.en: I can't survive on £40 a week (= it is not enough for my basic needs).
ex.cn: 一星期 40 英镑，我无法维持生活。

senses.def: to continue to live or exist despite a dangerous event or time
senses.chn: 幸存；幸免于难；艰难度过

ex.en: The company managed to survive the crisis.
ex.cn: 公司设法渡过了危机。

ex.en: Many birds didn't survive the severe winter.
ex.cn: 很多鸟死于这次严冬。

ex.en: Few buildings survived the war intact.
ex.cn: 战争之后没几座完好的建筑了。

senses.def: to live or exist longer than sb/sth

ex.en: She survived her husband by ten years.
ex.cn: 丈夫死后她又活了十年。

example.en: Some strange customs have survived from earlier times.
example.cn: 有些奇怪的风俗是从早年留存下来的。

example.en: I can't survive on £40 a week (= it is not enough for my basic needs).
example.cn: 一星期 40 英镑，我无法维持生活。

example.en: He survived as party leader until his second election defeat.
example.cn: 直至第二次参选失败他才不再担任党的领导人。

example.en: The company managed to survive the crisis.
example.cn: 公司设法渡过了危机。

example.en: Few buildings survived the war intact.
example.cn: 战争之后没几座完好的建筑了。

senses.def: a person who continues to live, especially despite being nearly killed or experiencing great danger or difficulty
senses.chn: 幸存者；生还者；挺过困难者

ex.en: the sole/only survivor of the massacre
ex.cn: 那场大屠杀的唯一幸存者

ex.en: The plane crashed in an area of dense jungle. There were no survivors.
ex.cn: 飞机坠落在一个丛林茂密的地区，无人生还。

ex.en: There are only a few survivors from the original team (= members who remain in it while others have been replaced).
ex.cn: 最初的队员只剩下几名了。

ex.en: She'll cope. She's one of life's great survivors (= sb who deals very well with difficult situations).
ex.cn: 她能挺过去。生活中什么样的困难她都能对付。

senses.def: the state of being very likely to be influenced, harmed or affected by sth
senses.chn: 易受影响（或伤害等）的特性；敏感性；过敏性

ex.en: susceptibility to disease
ex.cn: 易患病的体质

senses.def: a person's feelings which are likely to be easily hurt

ex.en: It was all carried out without any consideration for the susceptibilities of the bereaved family.
ex.cn: 这样做全然没有考虑到死者家人的感受。

senses.def: very likely to be influenced, harmed or affected by sb/sth
senses.chn: 易受影响（或伤害等）；敏感；过敏

ex.en: He's highly susceptible to flattery.
ex.cn: 他爱听恭维话。

ex.en: Some of these plants are more susceptible to frost damage than others.
ex.cn: 这些植物中有一些较其他的易受霜冻危害。

ex.en: Salt intake may lead to raised blood pressure in susceptible adults.
ex.cn: 盐的摄入可能导致易病的成年人血压升高。

senses.def: easily influenced by feelings and emotions
senses.chn: 好动感情的；感情丰富的；善感的

ex.en: She was both charming and susceptible.
ex.cn: 她迷人而多情。

senses.def: allowing sth; capable of sth

ex.en: Is this situation not susceptible of improvement by legislation?
ex.cn: 这种状况有没有可能通过立法加以改善？

senses.def: a Japanese dish of small cakes of cold cooked rice, flavoured with vinegar and served with raw fish, etc. on top
senses.chn: 寿司（日本食物，小糕饼状冷米饭配生鱼片等）

ex.en: a sushi bar
ex.cn: 寿司店

senses.def: to have an idea that sth is probably true or likely to happen, especially sth bad, but without having definite proof
senses.chn: 疑有，觉得（尤指坏事可能属实或发生）

ex.en: If you suspect a gas leak, do not strike a match or even turn on an electric light.
ex.cn: 假如你怀疑有煤气泄漏，不要划火柴，甚至连电灯都不要开。

ex.en: Suspecting nothing, he walked right into the trap.
ex.cn: 他毫无觉察，径直走入陷阱。

ex.en: As I had suspected all along, he was not a real policeman.
ex.cn: 他并不是真的警察，我一直就觉得不像。

ex.en: I began to suspect (that) they were trying to get rid of me.
ex.cn: 我开始觉察出，他们试图摆脱我。

ex.en: It was suspected that the drugs had been brought into the country by boat.
ex.cn: 有人怀疑毒品是用船运入该国的。

ex.en: She suspected him to be an impostor.
ex.cn: 她怀疑他是个冒名行骗者。

senses.def: to have an idea that sb is guilty of sth, without having definite proof

ex.en: He resigned after being suspected of theft.
ex.cn: 他被怀疑偷窃，随后就辞职了。

ex.en: The drug is suspected of causing over 200 deaths.
ex.cn: 人们怀疑这种药物造成 200 多人死亡。

ex.en: Whom do the police suspect?
ex.cn: 警方怀疑谁？

senses.def: to be suspicious about sth; to not trust sth
senses.chn: 怀疑；感觉有问题；不信任

ex.en: I suspected her motives in offering to help.
ex.cn: 她主动要帮忙，我怀疑她的动机。

senses.def: a person who is suspected of a crime or of having done sth wrong
senses.chn: 嫌疑犯；嫌疑分子；可疑对象

ex.en: a murder suspect
ex.cn: 杀人嫌疑犯

ex.en: He is the prime suspect in the case.
ex.cn: 他是这个案子的首要嫌疑人。

senses.def: that may be false and that cannot be relied on

ex.en: Some of the evidence they produced was highly suspect.
ex.cn: 他们出示的证据中有些相当成问题。

senses.def: that you suspect to be dangerous or illegal
senses.chn: 可疑的；可能有危险的；有违法嫌疑的

ex.en: a suspect package (= one that may contain drugs, a bomb, etc.)
ex.cn: 可疑包裹

example.en: If you suspect a gas leak, do not strike a match or even turn on an electric light.
example.cn: 假如你怀疑有煤气泄漏，不要划火柴，甚至连电灯都不要开。

example.en: I began to suspect (that) they were trying to get rid of me.
example.cn: 我开始觉察出，他们试图摆脱我。

example.en: It was suspected that the drugs had been brought into the country by boat.
example.cn: 有人怀疑毒品是用船运入该国的。

example.en: She suspected him to be an impostor.
example.cn: 她怀疑他是个冒名行骗者。

example.en: He resigned after being suspected of theft.
example.cn: 他被怀疑偷窃，随后就辞职了。

example.en: Whom do the police suspect?
example.cn: 警方怀疑谁？

senses.def: to hang sth from sth else

ex.en: A lamp was suspended from the ceiling.
ex.cn: 一盏吊灯悬在天花板上。

ex.en: Her body was found suspended by a rope.
ex.cn: 人们发现她的尸体吊在绳子上。

senses.def: to officially stop sth for a time; to prevent sth from being active, used, etc. for a time
senses.chn: 暂停；中止；使暂停发挥作用（或使用等）

ex.en: Production has been suspended while safety checks are carried out.
ex.cn: 在进行安全检查期间生产暂停。

ex.en: The constitution was suspended as the fighting grew worse.
ex.cn: 鉴于战斗趋于激烈，宪法暂停实施。

ex.en: In the theatre we willingly suspend disbelief (= temporarily believe that the characters, etc. are real).
ex.cn: 在剧院看戏时，我们自愿对一切暂不置疑。

senses.def: to officially delay sth; to arrange for sth to happen later than planned

ex.en: The introduction of the new system has been suspended until next year.
ex.cn: 新制度推迟到明年再行实施。

ex.en: to suspend judgement (= delay forming or expressing an opinion)
ex.cn: 暂不判断

senses.def: to officially prevent sb from doing their job, going to school, etc. for a time

ex.en: The police officer was suspended while the complaint was investigated.
ex.cn: 投诉调查期间，这名警员被暂停职务。

senses.def: to float in liquid or air without moving
the state of being alive but not conscious or active
a feeling that you cannot do anything because you are waiting for sth to happen
a punishment given to a criminal in court which means that they will only go to prison if they commit another crime within a particular period of time
a short circle of elastic for holding up a sock or stocking
long narrow pieces of cloth, leather, etc. for holding trousers/pants up. They are fastened to the top of the trousers/pants at the front and back and passed over the shoulders.
a piece of women's underwear like a belt, worn around the waist, used for holding stockings up
a feeling of worry or excitement that you have when you feel that sth is going to happen, sb is going to tell you some news, etc.
senses.chn: （对即将发生的事等的）担心；焦虑；兴奋；悬念

ex.en: a tale of mystery and suspense
ex.cn: 一个神秘莫测、充满悬念的故事

ex.en: Don't keep us in suspense. Tell us what happened!
ex.cn: 别让我们心老悬着了，告诉我们出了什么事！

ex.en: I couldn't bear the suspense a moment longer.
ex.cn: 这样提心吊胆，我一刻也受不了了。

senses.def: the act of officially removing sb from their job, school, team, etc. for a period of time, usually as a punishment
senses.chn: 暂令停职（或停学、停赛等）

ex.en: suspension from school
ex.cn: 暂被停学

ex.en: The two players are appealing against their suspensions.
ex.cn: 这两名运动员请求取消对他们的停赛处罚。

senses.def: the act of delaying sth for a period of time, until a decision has been taken

ex.en: These events have led to the suspension of talks.
ex.cn: 这些事件导致谈判延期。

senses.def: the system by which a vehicle is supported on its wheels and which makes it more comfortable to ride in when the road surface is not even
a liquid with very small pieces of solid matter floating in it; the state of such a liquid
a bridge that hangs from steel cables that are supported by towers at each end
a feeling that sb has done sth wrong, illegal or dishonest, even though you have no proof

ex.en: They drove away slowly to avoid arousing suspicion.
ex.cn: 他们缓缓驾车离去，以免引起怀疑。

ex.en: He was arrested on suspicion of murder.
ex.cn: 他因涉嫌谋杀而被捕。

ex.en: I have a sneaking suspicion that she's not telling the truth.
ex.cn: 我暗自怀疑她没讲实话。

senses.def: a feeling or belief that sth is true, even though you have no proof

ex.en: I have a horrible suspicion that we've come to the wrong station.
ex.cn: 我感觉不妙，我们可能来错车站了。

senses.def: the feeling that you cannot trust sb/sth

ex.en: Their offer was greeted with some suspicion.
ex.cn: 他们的主动热情遭到一些猜疑。

senses.def: a small amount of sth

ex.en: His mouth quivered in the suspicion of a smile.
ex.cn: 他嘴唇微微一颤，露出一丝笑意。

senses.def: too good, honest, etc. to have done sth wrong, illegal or dishonest

ex.en: Nobody who was near the scene of the crime is above suspicion.
ex.cn: 犯罪现场附近的任何人都不能排除嫌疑。

senses.def: suspected of doing sth wrong, illegal or dishonest

ex.en: The whole family is currently under suspicion of her murder.
ex.cn: 目前这一家人都涉嫌谋杀她。

ex.en: A number of doctors came under suspicion of unethical behaviour.
ex.cn: 一些医生涉嫌有不道德行为。

senses.def: if the finger of suspicion points or is pointed at sb, they are suspected of having committed a crime, being responsible for sth, etc.

example.en: I have a sneaking suspicion that she's not telling the truth.
example.cn: 我暗自怀疑她没讲实话。

senses.def: feeling that sb has done sth wrong, illegal or dishonest, without having any proof

ex.en: They became suspicious of his behaviour and contacted the police.
ex.cn: 他们开始觉得他行为可疑，便报了警。

ex.en: a suspicious look
ex.cn: 怀疑的神情

ex.en: You have a very suspicious mind (= you always think that people are behaving in an illegal or dishonest way).
ex.cn: 你疑心很重。

senses.def: making you feel that sth is wrong, illegal or dishonest

ex.en: Didn't you notice anything suspicious in his behaviour?
ex.cn: 你难道没有注意到他行为有可疑之处？

ex.en: She died in suspicious circumstances.
ex.cn: 她死得蹊跷。

ex.en: Police are not treating the fire as suspicious.
ex.cn: 警方认为这场火灾没有可疑之处。

ex.en: It was all very suspicious.
ex.cn: 这一切十分可疑。

senses.def: not willing or able to trust sb/sth
senses.chn: 不信任的；持怀疑态度的

ex.en: I was suspicious of his motives.
ex.cn: 我怀疑他的动机。

ex.en: Many were suspicious of reform.
ex.cn: 很多人对改革持怀疑态度。

senses.def: in a way that shows you think sb has done sth wrong, illegal or dishonest

ex.en: The man looked at her suspiciously.
ex.cn: 那个男人以狐疑的目光看着她。

senses.def: in a way that makes people think sth wrong, illegal or dishonest is happening
senses.chn: 令人怀疑地；形迹（或神色等）可疑地

ex.en: Let me know if you see anyone acting suspiciously.
ex.cn: 如发现有人形迹可疑，你就告诉我。

senses.def: in a way that shows you think there may be sth wrong with sth
senses.chn: 以怀疑的态度；不信任地

ex.en: She eyed the fish on her plate suspiciously.
ex.cn: 她不放心地看着自己盘子里的鱼。

senses.def: to be very similar to sth
senses.chn: 看／听上去与某事物相像得令人起疑

ex.en: Their latest single sounds suspiciously like the last one.
ex.cn: 他们的最新单曲唱片听着和前一张很像。

senses.def: to realize sth; to understand the important things about sb/sth

ex.en: I think I've got him sussed (= now I understand him).
ex.cn: 我想我已了解他了。

ex.en: If you want to succeed in business you have to suss out the competition.
ex.cn: 要想在生意场上立足，你必须真正明白竞争是怎么回事。

ex.en: He cheated on her for years, but she never sussed.
ex.cn: 他有外遇多年了，但她从来没有察觉。

senses.def: knowing what you need to know about the situations and people around you, so that you are not easily tricked and are able to take care of yourself
senses.chn: 有（处世）经验而不易上当的；门槛精的

senses.def: to provide enough of what sb/sth needs in order to live or exist

ex.en: Which planets can sustain life?
ex.cn: 哪些行星可以维持生命的存在？

ex.en: The love and support of his family sustained him during his time in prison.
ex.cn: 家人的关爱和支持帮助他度过了狱中的岁月。

senses.def: to make sth continue for some time without becoming less

ex.en: a period of sustained economic growth
ex.cn: 经济持续增长的时期

ex.en: a sustained attack
ex.cn: 持续的攻击

ex.en: She managed to sustain everyone's interest until the end of her speech.
ex.cn: 她使每个人兴趣盎然，一直听她把话讲完。

senses.def: to experience sth bad

ex.en: to sustain damage/an injury/a defeat
ex.cn: 遭受损失；受伤；遭到失败

ex.en: The company sustained losses of millions of dollars.
ex.cn: 公司遭受了数百万美元计的巨大损失。

senses.def: to provide evidence to support an opinion, a theory, etc.

ex.en: The evidence is not detailed enough to sustain his argument.
ex.cn: 这一证据过于笼统，不足以证明他的论点。

senses.def: to support a weight without breaking or falling

ex.en: The ice will not sustain your weight.
ex.cn: 这冰承受不了你的体重。

senses.def: to decide that a claim, etc. is valid

ex.en: The court sustained his claim that the contract was illegal.
ex.cn: 法庭支持他的主张，认定该合同不合法。

ex.en: Objection sustained!(= said by a judge when a lawyer makes an objection in court)
ex.cn: 反对有效！

senses.def: involving the use of natural products and energy in a way that does not harm the environment
senses.chn: （对自然资源和能源的利用）不破坏生态平衡的，合理利用的

ex.en: sustainable forest management
ex.cn: 合理的森林管理

ex.en: an environmentally sustainable society
ex.cn: 保持生态环境平衡的社会

senses.def: that can continue or be continued for a long time

ex.en: sustainable economic growth
ex.cn: 经济的可持续增长

senses.def: the food and drink that people, animals and plants need to live and stay healthy

ex.en: There's not much sustenance in a bowl of soup.
ex.cn: 一碗汤没多少营养。

ex.en: Arguing would only give further sustenance to his allegations.
ex.cn: 越是争论，他越会觉得自己那些说法有道理。

senses.def: the process of making sth continue to exist

ex.en: Elections are essential for the sustenance of parliamentary democracy.
ex.cn: 选举制度是维持议会民主所必不可少的。

senses.def: a rule or statement in Sanskrit literature, or a set of rules
a Buddhist or Jainist holy text
a stitch or stitches made when sewing up a wound, especially after an operation
senses.chn: （尤指手术后伤口的）缝合，缝线

senses.def: to sew up a wound
the right of a country to rule over another country
thin and attractive
a person who has the power to control another person's mind, make them do bad things, etc.
senses.chn: 能控制他人思想的人；能使人干坏事（或唯命是从）的人

senses.def: short wave

ex.en: SW and LW radio
ex.cn: 短波及长波无线电设备

senses.def: south-west; south-western

ex.en: SW Australia
ex.cn: 澳大利亚西南部

senses.def: a piece of soft material used by a doctor, nurse, etc. for cleaning wounds or taking a sample from sb's body for testing
an act of taking a sample from sb's body, with a swab
senses.chn: 用拭子对（人体）化验标本的采集

ex.en: to take a throat swab
ex.cn: 用棉签从咽部采集化验样品

senses.def: to clean or remove liquid from a wound, etc., using a swab
to clean or wash a floor, surface, etc. using water and a cloth, etc.
to wrap sb/sth, especially a baby, tightly in clothes or a piece of cloth
senses.chn: （用衣服或布）紧裹，包裹（尤指婴儿）

senses.def: strips of cloth used in the past for wrapping a baby tightly
made in India from materials that have also been produced in India
goods that have been stolen
cloth that is hung in large curved folds as decoration, especially above a window
senses.chn: （挂于窗户等上方的）装饰性布幔（或帷幕）

senses.def: a pack of things tied or wrapped together and carried by a traveller
a bunch of flowers or fruit that is carved onto walls, etc. as decoration
senses.chn: 垂花饰（雕刻装饰，形状为串起来的花、果等）

senses.def: to walk in an extremely proud and confident way
senses.chn: 神气十足地走；大摇大摆地走

senses.def: a way of walking or behaving that seems too confident
a man who travels around looking for work, carrying his possessions wrapped in a cloth
senses.chn: 背着行囊四处找工作的人

senses.def: a language widely used in E Africa, especially between people who speak different first languages
senses.chn: 斯瓦希里语（通行于东非，尤作第二语言）

senses.def: a young man who is in love
to make food, drink, etc. go down your throat into your stomach

ex.en: Always chew food well before swallowing it.
ex.cn: 什么食物都要先嚼碎再吞咽。

ex.en: I had a sore throat and it hurt to swallow.
ex.cn: 当时我嗓子疼，咽东西就疼。

ex.en: The pills should be swallowed whole.
ex.cn: 这些药要吞服。

senses.def: to move the muscles of your throat as if you were swallowing sth, especially because you are nervous

ex.en: She swallowed hard and told him the bad news.
ex.cn: 她使劲咽了口唾沫，把坏消息告诉了他。

senses.def: to take sb/sth in or completely cover it so that they cannot be seen or no longer exist separately

ex.en: I watched her walk down the road until she was swallowed by the darkness.
ex.cn: 我看着她沿公路越走越远，直至消失在黑暗中。

ex.en: Large areas of countryside have been swallowed up by towns.
ex.cn: 大片大片的乡村地区被城镇吞噬。

senses.def: to use up sth completely, especially an amount of money

ex.en: Most of my salary gets swallowed (up) by the rent and bills.
ex.cn: 我的工资大多支付房租和各种日常费用了。

senses.def: to accept that sth is true; to believe sth

ex.en: I found her excuse very hard to swallow.
ex.cn: 我觉得她的理由很难让人相信。

ex.en: He told her a pack of lies, but she swallowed it whole.
ex.cn: 他对她讲了一堆假话，可她全都信以为真。

senses.def: to hide your feelings

ex.en: to swallow your doubts
ex.cn: 不流露怀疑

ex.en: You're going to have to swallow your pride and ask for your job back.
ex.cn: 你得放下架子，去求人家给你恢复原职。

senses.def: to accept insults, criticisms, etc. without complaining or protesting

ex.en: I was surprised that he just sat there and swallowed all their remarks.
ex.cn: 让我吃惊的是他就坐在那儿默默地任凭他们评论。

senses.def: a fact or an event that is unpleasant and difficult to accept
senses.chn: 严酷的现实；（难以咽下的）苦果

senses.def: a small bird with long pointed wings and a tail with two points, that spends the winter in Africa but flies to northern countries for the summer
an act of swallowing; an amount of food or drink that is swallowed at one time
senses.chn: 咽；吞；一次吞咽的量；一口

senses.def: you must not take too seriously a small sign that sth is happening or will happen in the future, because the situation could change
senses.chn: 别略有好事就以为佳时已到；好事可能纯属偶然；一燕不成夏（不能单凭微小的迹象而下定论）

example.en: Always chew food well before swallowing it.
example.cn: 什么食物都要先嚼碎再吞咽。

example.en: The pills should be swallowed whole.
